title: Introduction to computer
content:
Definition of computer:

The term computer derived from a Latin word " Compute" which means to calculate. So "A computer is normally considerd to be an calculating device as well as electronic device that can perform mathmatical(arithmatical/logical operation) with high speed and accuracy."

OR

Computer is an electronic data processing machine, which accept raw data  from user as input , process and displays it in the form of output.

A computer  used by a particular person, called personal computer (micro computer) or PC. All those computers, which are used at home, office or business, are microcomputers.Personal  computers can be many types.A personal computer may be desktop, laptop,tablet etc.

How computer works ?

A computer works on the concept of IPO (Input- Processing-Output)

Characteristics of computer: 

The increasing popularity of computers has proved that it is a very powerful and useful. The characterstics of a computer are as follows:

  • Speed : A computer is a very fast device.Billions of complex arithmatical operations can be performed in a microseconds or nano seconds.
  • Accuracy: Every calculation is performed with almost complete accuracy.
  • Dilligence: A computer is free from tiredness and boredome; it can work for 24 hours without becoming tired.
  • Automatic: Computers are automatic machines because, once started on a job, they carry on until the job is finished without human assitance.
  • Versatility: They can perform multiple tasks at the same time and are flexiblle enough to perform both simple and complex tasks.
  • Storage capacity: Any data can be stored in computer in any form and quantity. Data can be stored for a longer period and can be obtain as per our needs.
  • Plug and play: They can automatically configure new hardware and software.

Limitations: Limitations are the drawbacks of the computeer system in which humans outperform them. A computer system has following limitations:

  • Zero IQ(Intelligence Quotients): They have zero IQ.They are unable to see and think the  actions to perform in a particular situation unless that situation is already programmed into them.
  • Lack of decision-making: Decision-making is a complicated process involving information, knowledge, intelligence, wisdom and ability to judge.The computer system does not have the ability to make decisions on their own.
  • Lack of common sense: Computers, function based on the stored programs and they simply lack common sense.

title: Types of Computer
content:
Types of computer: The classification of computer based on work system is as follows:

Digital computer: 

  • Digital computers present all data in digits and perform all activties on the basis of digits.
  • These computers perform all the functions using the digits 0 and 1.
  • This types of computer are used for personal, commercial and research laboratories.
  • Ex: Calculator , Smartphone , Laptop, Desktop etc .

These computers are of four types based on their size, which are explained as follows:

1. Micro computer: 

  • In the year 1971, Intel corporation invented Microprocessor chip first time. E.D. Robert developed the first Micro computer.
  • All those computers who use the microprocessor as main components are called Micro computer.
  • Desktop computer,Personal computer,Note Book, Tablets PC, Handheld((PDA & Smart phone) are some common examples of Micro computer.

 

2. Mini computer: 

  • It's processor is small but larger than microcomputer.
  • This type of computer are smaller in size and are more powerful than microcomputer and it is multiuser device, used to carry out some specific task in engineering and computer added  design(CAD). 

3. Main Frame computer: 

  • Their processing capacity of Main frame computer is more than mini computers.
  • It is used as server in computer network and they are made for multiuser environment.
  • Therefore, it has more storage and processing capacity.
  • It is used mainly for scientific experiments and complex calculations.

4. Super computer: 

  • It is the fastest, most expansive machine available today and use for complex matematical calculations .
  • Super computers are used in weather forecasting ,rocket launching and nuclear research.
  • They are expensive; therefore, these are used for special tasks. Indian PARAM and IBM's Blue Gene are some  examples of super computers.

*FLOPS: Floating point operations per second or FLOPS is the Unite of measurement that the performance & capability of a super computer.

Analog computer:

  •   Analog computers are special types of computers.
  • They work on the basis of special signals like temperature, pressure,speed or electric flow etc. 

 Hybrid computer: 

  • These computers are the combination of Digital and Analog computers.
  • So, they work on the signals of temperature, pressure etc.
  • They work on the basis of digits of digits also.
  • Ex: ECG machine , ultra sound machine etc.

Applications of computer:

  • Commercial use
  • Medical science
  • Education
  • Research
  • Transport(Railways)
  • Enterainment
  • Banking
  • Technology
  • Personal use
  • Defence

title: What is Computation?
content:
Topic -1 - What is Computation?

Computation just means how we tell a computer to solve a problem step by step. Think of it like giving instructions to a robot:

  • "Take one step forward."
  • "Turn left."
  • "Pick up the ball."

That’s computation! So the basic model of computation in programming refers to a formal framework (Structure) for understanding how algorithms and computational processes work. At its core, it represents the fundamental principles by which problems are solved and computations are performed. Various models of computation provide different perspectives on how programs are executed and how problems are solved efficiently.

Models of Computation: A model of computation is like a set of rules that says how a computer/robot can follow instructions.

            Here are the key models of computation in programming:

        Turing Machine: A Turing Machine is a theoretical model of computation introduced by Alan Turing in 1936. It consists of an infinite tape, a tape head that reads and writes symbols on the tape and moves left or right , and a finite set of states that Describes what the machine does (read, write, move, change state) based on the current state and symbol.

              A Turing Machine can perform any calculation that is computable, meaning any problem solvable by an algorithm can be solved by a Turing Machine (this is known as Turing completeness).

Finite State Machine (FSM) : A Finite State Machine is a computational model used for designing systems with a limited number of states. The machine transitions between different states based on input (alphabet) symbols.

        FSMs have a finite set of states and are more limited than Turing Machines, making them less powerful, but easier to analyze for certain types of tasks (e.g., recognizing patterns or making decisions based on simple inputs).

    Example of Finite State Machine (FSM)

  • Imagine a traffic light. It can only be in a few states: Red, Green, or Yellow.
  • Rules decide how it switches (Red → Green → Yellow → Red).
  • Computers use FSM for simple tasks like vending machines.

Lambda Calculus : Lambda Calculus, introduced by Alonzo Church in the 1930s, is a formal system for expressing computation based on function abstraction and application. It serves as the foundation of functional programming languages like Haskell, Lisp, and Scala.

          Computation is modelled as the evaluation of mathematical functions, and it provides a way to express complex transformations and recursive algorithms.

Example: solving problems with pure math functions.

 Pushdown Automaton (PDA):  A Pushdown Automaton is a type of computational model that extends finite state machines by adding a stack to store additional information. PDAs are used to recognize context-free languages and are critical for parsing programming languages and designing compilers.

        Unlike FSMs, PDAs can handle a stack, which makes them more powerful, allowing them to recognize more complex patterns, such as balanced parentheses or nested structures.

Register Machines: A register machine is a model of computation that works with a finite number of registers (storage locations), and operations on these registers represent the computation.

Von Neumann Architecture (or Stored Program Concept) :  The Von Neumann architecture is a design for a computer system where both data and program instructions are stored in memory. It uses a central processing unit (CPU), memory, and input/output systems to execute instructions.

Model of Computation in Functional Programming: In functional programming, the model of computation is based on the evaluation of mathematical functions, immutability, and higher-order functions (functions that take other functions as arguments or return them as results).

Parallel Computation Models: These models extend traditional models to account for multiple processors or computing units working together on a problem. Examples include the PRAM (Parallel Random Access Machine) and Bulk Synchronous Parallel (BSP) models.

Actor Model: The Actor Model is a conceptual model where "actors" are the fundamental units of computation. Each actor can receive a message, process it, and send messages to other actors.

Note: These models of computation provide diverse ways of thinking about and solving problems in computer science. While the Turing Machine is the most general and powerful theoretical model, simpler models like finite state machines or pushdown automata are useful for practical applications such as compilers and pattern recognition. The choice of model depends on the complexity and nature of the problem being solved, with each offering a different perspective on computation.

title: Basic Model of Computation
content:
The Basic Model of Computation:

A program is a set of instructions, written in a computer language, to perform a specific task. to solve problems on a computer, one has to write a step-by-step solution using simple instructions for operations and thus, obtain the results. There would be a number of methods to solve a given problem, and therefore, solutions may differ from person to person. However, in all cases, the basic steps remain the same.

These basic steps are as follows:

1.         Formulating the problem and deciding the data types to be inputted.

2.         Identifying the steps of computation that are necessary for getting the solution.

3.         Identifying decision points, i.e., under what circumstances a particular operation is to be performed and when not to be performed.

4.         Knowing the expected results and verifying with the actual values.

Procedure for Problem Solving:

Problem-solving is the process involving basic sequential steps necessary to arrive at the solution of the given problem. It is a logical process of breaking down the problem into small parts which can be solved step by step to obtain the result. This does not involve the computer.

Though every problem is unique in itself, a few basic steps for solving the problem are common. These steps should be understood thoroughly and practiced effectively. Using these steps, your problem-solving capability will improve with time. The six basic steps in solving a problem are as follows:

Step 1. Understanding the Problem:

Spend some time understanding the problem thoroughly. In this step, you are not required to use the computer. Instead, you should try to answer what is expected and how to obtain it. This means, try to solve the problem manually.

Step 2. Construction of the List of Variables

Construct a list of variables that are needed to get the solution to the problem. Means we should think in advance about the number of variables required and the name of the variables before drawing the flowchart. The names chosen for variables should be an aid to memory.

Step 3. Output Design:

Decide the layout for the output presentation, it may not be so. If the output format is not specified, you must keep in mind that the output report should easily be understandable to a reader. The output format should have the following characteristics:

  • Attractive
  • Easy-to-read
  • Self-explanatory

Step 4. Program Development:

      Select the programming technique which is best suited to solve the problem and, then only carry out the coding, using a suitable programming language.  You should now draw a flowchart for the procedure that you have just made in Steps 1, 2, and 3. Standard symbols should be used for drawing the flowchart. If the problem is complex, you should divide it into several simpler parts. Then, draw a flowchart for each part separately and join them together using connectors.

Step 5. Testing the Program:

Test the program Select test data so that each part of the program can be checked for correctness. We should give a dry run to the program developed in Step 4. This means giving some known values to the variables and checking the result by comparing them with manually calculated values. Test values are selected such that each part of the flowchart is tested, and consequently, the program is confirmed to be free from any logical errors.

Step 6. Validating the Data

Finally, use data validation steps to prevent the processing of wrongly entered data.

The above mentioned six steps are further elaborated in the following sections: It is quite likely that the user of our program may enter values that are not expected by the program. Such values should be rejected by the procedure created by us. This is known as validation of data.

Problem Definition and use of Examples for Problem-Solving:

Let us take an example of a problem faced in day-to-day life. Suppose, you want to reach your computer Canter by 10 AM. You would lay out a plan to get ready by 9 AM; then take a bus/rickshaw to reach the gate of your Institute. Then, climb up the stairs to arrive at the laboratory. You will note the time taken for each part. If due to some reason, you are unable to get ready by 9 AM, and you already know that it takes one hour to reach the Institute Lab by bus/rickshaw, then you will take a faster means of transportation. You may take a Bike or a taxi. Thus, a very simple problem of reaching the computer lab by 10 AM will need several steps to reach a solution. Each step is to be accurately defined/marked so that no guesswork is required.

title: Algorithms & Flowcharts
content:
Topic -3  - Algorithms & Flowcharts

Algorithms:  An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure or set of rules used to perform a specific task or solve a problem. Algorithms form the foundation of computer programming and are critical for efficiently processing data, solving problems, and performing computations. And it is the heart and soul of programming .

Flowchart: A flowchart is a visual representation of the steps or the flow of a process  involved in solving a problem or performing a task. It uses a standardized set of symbols to depict the flow of control and operations within a system. Flowcharts are commonly used in programming, algorithm design, and process modeling to help understand and communicate complex processes in a clear, easy-to-follow manner.

Programming Languages:  A programming language is a formal set of instructions that a computer can understand and execute. It provides a way for programmers to write software, automate tasks, and create applications. Programming languages are the foundation of software development

Types of Programming Languages

1. Low-Level Languages

  • Machine Language (Binary code)
  • Assembly Language (Mnemonics like MOV A, B)

2. High-Level Languages (Easier to read and write)

  • Procedural: C, Pascal
  • Object-Oriented: Java, Python, C++
  • Functional: Lisp, Haskell
  • Scripting: Python, JavaScript

Specialized Programming Languages : Some languages are designed for specific domains or applications:

  • Web Development:
    • HTML, CSS (markup & styling)
    • JavaScript, TypeScript
    • PHP, Ruby, Python (Django, Flask)
    • Node.js (JavaScript for backend)
  • Mobile Development:
    • Swift (iOS)
    • Kotlin (Android)
    • Java (Legacy Android)
    • Dart (Flutter framework for cross-platform)
  • Game Development:
    • C++ (Unreal Engine)
    • C# (Unity)
    • Python (Pygame)
    • Lua (Roblox, Corona SDK)
  • Data Science & Machine Learning:
    • Python (TensorFlow, PyTorch, Pandas)
    • R (Statistical computing)
    • Julia (High-performance computing)
  • Systems Programming:
    • C (Operating systems, embedded systems)
    • Rust (Memory-safe systems programming)
    • Go (Concurrency-heavy applications)
  • Database & Query Languages:
    • SQL (Structured Query Language)
    • NoSQL (MongoDB, Cassandra)
    • PL/SQL (Oracle-specific SQL extensions)
  • Embedded Systems & IoT:
    • C, C++
    • MicroPython
    • Rust
    • Assembly
  • Cybersecurity & Ethical Hacking:
    • Python (Automation, scripting)
    • C (Low-level exploits)
    • Bash (Linux automation)
    • Assembly (Reverse engineering)
  • Functional Programming Languages:
    • Haskell
    • Lisp
    • Elixir
    • F#

 Emerging & Trending Languages

  • Rust: Gaining traction for system-level programming due to memory safety.
  • Go: Popular in cloud computing and microservices.
  • Dart: Used in Flutter for mobile and web applications.
  • Julia: Rising in data science and scientific computing.

Compilation in Programming Languages: Compilation is the process of converting human-readable source code into machine code (binary instructions) that a computer can execute. This is done using a compiler, which translates the entire program before execution.

Steps in Compilation:

  1. Pre-processing:
    • The pre-processor handles directives (like #include and #define in C/C++).
    • It removes comments, expands macros, and includes files.
  2. Lexical Analysis:
    • The lexer (or scanner) breaks the source code into tokens, which are the smallest units of meaning (keywords, operators, identifiers, etc.).
  3. Syntax Analysis:
    • The parser checks if the tokens form a valid syntax according to the language's grammar.
    • It produces a syntax tree or Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) that represents the hierarchical structure of the source code.
  4. Semantic Analysis:
    • This stage checks for semantic errors, such as type mismatches, undeclared variables, etc.
    • It also annotates the AST with additional information needed for code generation.
  5. Intermediate Code Generation:
    • The compiler generates an intermediate representation (IR) of the source code that is easier to optimize.
    • The IR is independent of both the source language and the target machine.
  6. Optimization:
    • The compiler optimizes the intermediate code to improve performance and reduce memory usage.
    • Optimization techniques include constant folding, loop unrolling, and dead code elimination.
  7. Code Generation:
    • The compiler translates the optimized intermediate code into machine code specific to the target architecture.
    • This involves allocating memory, assigning registers, and generating assembly instructions.
  8. Assembly:
    • The assembler converts the generated assembly code into object code, which is in a binary format that the computer can execute.
    • Object files contain machine code and additional information (e.g., symbol tables) needed for linking.
  9. Linking:
    • The linker combines object files and libraries into a single executable.
    • It resolves references to external symbols and addresses.
  10. Loading and Execution:
    • The loader loads the executable into memory and prepares it for execution.
    • The operating system then starts executing the program.

title: Testing & Debugging
content:
Topic - 4  Testing & Debugging :

Testing and debugging are crucial parts of the software development process. They ensure that your code works as intended and is free of errors. Here's an overview of both:

Testing: Testing involves checking your code to verify that it behaves as expected. There are several types of testing:

 

  1. Unit Testing:
    • Tests individual units or components of a program.
    • Ensures that each unit functions correctly in isolation.
    • Example: Testing a single function or method.
  2. Integration Testing:
    • Tests the interaction between different units or components.
    • Ensures that combined components work together as expected.
    • Example: Testing multiple functions or modules together.
  3. System Testing:
    • Tests the entire system as a whole.
    • Ensures that the system meets the specified requirements.
    • Example: Testing a complete application.
  4. Acceptance Testing:
    • Tests the system for acceptability.
    • Ensures that the system meets the user's requirements.
    • Example: User testing before product release.
  5. Regression Testing:
    • Tests to ensure that new changes have not introduced any new bugs.
    • Example: Re-running previous tests after a code update.
  6. Performance Testing:
    • Tests how well the system performs under various conditions.
    • Example: Load testing to see how the system handles a high number of users.

Debugging: Debugging is the process of finding and fixing errors or bugs in your code. Here's how to approach debugging:

  1. Identify the Problem:
    • Understand the symptoms of the bug.
    • Reproduce the issue consistently.
  2. Isolate the Cause:
    • Narrow down the part of the code causing the problem.
    • Use debugging tools like breakpoints and step-by-step execution.
  2. Fix the Issue:
    • Modify the code to resolve the problem.
    • Ensure that the fix does not introduce new bugs.
  3. Test the Fix:
    • Run tests to ensure the issue is resolved.
    • Perform regression testing to ensure no new issues are introduced.
  4. Review the Code:
    • Look for potential issues in the modified code.
    • Use code reviews and static analysis tools.

Note : Testing and debugging are essential skills for any programmer. They help ensure that your code is reliable, efficient, and maintainable. If you need more detailed information or examples, just let me know!

title: Documentation
content:
Topic - 5 - Documentation:

Documentation is absolutely crucial in the world of programming and software development. It serves as the bridge between code and understanding, ensuring that software is maintainable, usable, and reliable. Here's a breakdown of its importance and types:

Why Documentation Matters:

  • Understanding Code:
    • It explains the "why" behind the "what" of your code, making it easier for others (and your future self) to understand its purpose and functionality.
  • Maintenance and Collaboration:
    • Well-written documentation simplifies debugging, updating, and extending code, especially in collaborative projects.
    • It enables team members to quickly grasp the codebase and contribute effectively.
  • Usability:
    • User-facing documentation, like user manuals and API documentation, guides users on how to interact with and utilize software.
  • Knowledge Sharing:
    • It preserves institutional knowledge, preventing information loss when developers leave a project.
  • Testing and Quality Assurance:
    • Documentation helps testers understand the expected behavior of the software, facilitating thorough testing.
  • Legal and Compliance:
    • In some industries, documentation is required for regulatory compliance.

Types of Documentation:

  • Code Comments: Inline explanations within the code itself, clarifying specific sections or functions.
  • API Documentation: Describes how to use an Application Programming Interface (API), outlining its endpoints, parameters, and responses.
  • User Manuals: Guides users on how to install, configure, and use software applications.
  • Technical Specifications: Detailed descriptions of the software's design, architecture, and technical requirements.
  • Software Design Documents: explains the design choices made while developing the software.
  • README Files: Short, introductory documents that provide essential information about a project, such as installation instructions and usage examples.
  • Tutorials and Guides: Step-by-step instructions and examples that help users learn how to use a software product or library.
  • Architectural Documentation: Describes the high-level structure of the software system.

title: Introduction of The Internet
content:
What is the Internet?

The Internet is a vast system of networks that connects millions of private, public, academic, business, and government networks. These networks utilize the Internet Protocol Suite (TCP/IP) to link devices worldwide.

Key Features of the Internet:

  1. Global Connectivity
    The Internet allows for instant communication and access to information across the globe, bridging geographical boundaries.

  2. Distributed Network
    The structure of the Internet is decentralized, meaning no single entity controls it entirely, which makes it resilient to failures or attacks.

  3. Data Sharing
    It facilitates the exchange of data through various services, such as the World Wide Web (WWW), email, and file-sharing protocols.

  4. Scalability
    The Internet can support an increasing number of devices and services without significant performance degradation, making it future-proof.

  5. Interactivity
    With the advent of Web 2.0 technologies, the Internet has evolved to support highly interactive experiences through social media, online gaming, and collaborative tools.

Historical Background of the Internet

The concept of an interconnected global network dates back to the 1960s. The first practical implementation of this idea was ARPANET (Advanced Research Projects Agency Network), which was funded by the U.S. Department of Defense. By the late 1980s, the Internet began evolving into the network we recognize today.

Why is the Internet Important?

  • Global Communication: The Internet is the backbone of modern communication, enabling emails, instant messaging, and social networking.

  • Education: Access to online courses, tutorials, and research materials has revolutionized learning.

  • Commerce: E-commerce has transformed how businesses and consumers interact, with online shopping, digital payment systems, and services becoming integral.

  • Entertainment: Streaming services, online gaming, and social platforms offer limitless entertainment options.

title: Introduction to WWW
content:
🌐 World Wide Web (WWW)

The World Wide Web (WWW), also known simply as the Web, is the part of the internet that contains websites and web pages.

  • WWW is a collection of interconnected web pages, linked through hypertext and stored on web servers, which are accessed by local computers via the internet.

  • It works on a Client–Server Architecture, where documents are written in HTML (HyperText Markup Language).

  • The WWW was developed by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989 at CERN, Geneva, Switzerland.

👉 First Web Browser: Mosaic (1992)
👉 Popular Early Browser: Netscape Navigator (1994)

🌍 Difference Between Internet and WWW

  • Internet: A global network of interconnected computers and devices that communicate using protocols like TCP/IP. It provides the infrastructure for data transfer.

  • WWW: A service that runs on the internet, consisting of websites and web pages accessible via browsers using HTTP/HTTPS.

🔑 Components of WWW

  1. Web Browsers
    Applications like Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge, and Safari that retrieve, interpret, and display web content.

  2. HTML (HyperText Markup Language)
    The standard language for creating web pages, structuring content with headings, paragraphs, images, and links.

  3. CSS (Cascading Style Sheets)
    Defines the design and layout of web pages, including colors, fonts, and styles.

  4. JavaScript
    A programming language that enables dynamic and interactive features (e.g., form validation, animations, real-time updates).

  5. Web Servers
    Computers that store, process, and deliver web pages to browsers upon request.

  6. HTTP/HTTPS (HyperText Transfer Protocol / Secure)
    Protocols used for communication between browsers and servers.

    • HTTP: Standard protocol.

    • HTTPS: Secure protocol with encryption.

  7. URLs (Uniform Resource Locators)
    Addresses used to access specific web pages or resources.
    Example: https://www.example.com

  8. DNS (Domain Name System)
    Translates human-readable domain names (e.g., www.google.com) into IP addresses that computers use to identify each other.

📌 Elements of WWW

  • Website

  • Web Page

  • Hypertext

  • Hyperlinks

🖥️ Website

  • A website is a collection of interlinked web pages, associated with a person, business, school, government, or organization.

  • A website may consist of a single page or multiple pages containing information.

  • Websites provide a large amount of information and come in various types (e.g., education, jobs, e-commerce).

👉 To display a website on the internet, you need:

  1. A Website (content/pages)

  2. A Domain Name

  3. A Web Server

  4. (Additionally: PC, Web Browser, and Internet)

⚙️ How a Website Works

  1. Web Browser: A user types a domain name (e.g., www.example.com) in a browser like Chrome, Safari, or Firefox.

  2. DNS (Domain Name System): The DNS translates the domain name into an IP address, which points to the web server hosting the site.

  3. Request & Response: The browser sends a request to the server. The server processes it and sends back the website files (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images).

  4. Rendering: The browser renders these files and displays the website to the user

📄 Web Pages

  • A web page is an electronic document written in HTML.

  • It is accessible through the internet using a web browser.

  • Each web page has a unique address called a URL (Uniform Resource Locator).

  • The first page of any website is known as the homepage.

  • A web page can contain text, graphics, audio, video, and other multimedia content.

  • A web page is part of a website.

🔗 Hyperlinks

  • A hyperlink is a web navigation element that allows users to move or navigate between different web pages.

  • Hyperlinks can also be used to download files such as images, audio, and video.

  • They are usually displayed as blue underlined text (though the style can be customized).

Types of Hyperlinks:

  1. Text Hyperlink – Links created using text.

  2. Image Hyperlink – Links created using images.

  3. Image Maps – A single image divided into multiple clickable areas, each acting as a different link.

✨ Hypertext

  • Hypertext is text that contains hyperlinks.

  • When clicked, it connects to another page, resource, or section within the same page.

title: Frontend and Backend Development
content:
🌐 Frontend and Backend in Web Development

In web development, Frontend and Backend are the two main parts of any application. Together, they allow websites and web applications to function smoothly.

🎨 Frontend Development (Client-Side)

The Frontend is the part of a website or application that users see and interact with directly.

  • It manages everything that appears on the browser screen.

  • Also called the Client Side of development.

  • Built using core web technologies:

    • HTML → structures the content.

    • CSS → styles and layouts.

    • JavaScript → adds interactivity.

🔧 Popular Frontend Frameworks

  • React

  • Angular.js

⚙️ Backend Development (Server-Side)

The Backend is the part of a website or application that users cannot see. It handles the logic, data, and communication between the server and the client.

  • Runs on the server side.

  • Responsible for storing, arranging, and retrieving data from databases.

  • Ensures the Frontend works properly by processing user requests and sending responses.

  • Backend developers create the logic and functionality of apps/websites.

🔧 Popular Backend Languages & Frameworks

  • JavaScript (Node.js)

  • Python (Django, Flask)

  • PHP (Laravel, CodeIgniter)

  • Ruby (Rails)

  • Java (Spring)

  • C++

👉 Note: JavaScript can be used in both Frontend (React, Vue) and Backend (Node.js).

🖥️ Client-Side vs Server-Side Scripting

To understand web applications better, we must differentiate between Client-Side and Server-Side scripting:

📌 Client-Side Scripting

  • Executed inside the user’s browser.

  • Creates interactive and dynamic web pages.

  • Improves user experience by making apps more responsive.

  • Placed directly in HTML documents.

Examples:

  • HTML

  • CSS

  • JavaScript

📌 Server-Side Scripting

  • Executed on the web server (not on the user’s browser).

  • Handles data storage, retrieval, and server logic.

  • Establishes communication between server and client.

  • Generates dynamic content before sending it to the browser.

Examples:

  • JavaScript (Node.js)

  • Python

  • PHP

  • Ruby

  • Java

  • C++

title: Types of Websites
content:
🌐 Types of Websites

Websites can be broadly classified into two main types:

  1. Static Websites (client side)

  2. Dynamic Websites

📝 Static Websites

  • A Static Website displays fixed content that does not change unless manually updated by the webmaster.

  • Content remains constant or fixed for every visitor.

  • Built using HTML (sometimes with CSS for styling).

  • Does not require databases or programming knowledge.

  • Content changes only when the webmaster edits the code.

  • Cost-efficient → ideal for small businesses, personal portfolios, or basic company profiles.

⚙️ Dynamic Websites

A Dynamic Website displays content that can change automatically based on user interaction, time, or database updates.

  • Content is dynamic and interactive.

  • Retrieves information from a database or Content Management System (CMS).

  • When the database is updated, the website content changes automatically.

  • Built using server-side programming languages, such as:

    • PHP (Hypertext Preprocessor)

    • ASP (Active Server Page)

    • JSP (Java Server Page)

    • Ruby, etc.

  • Commonly used for e-commerce sites, blogs, forums, social networks, and news portals.

 Example: Amazon, Facebook, Online Banking, News Websites.

title: Responsive Web design
content:
📱 Responsive Web Designing

Responsive Web Designing is an approach to web design where a single website is created to automatically adjust its layout and content depending on the device being used (desktop, tablet, or smartphone).

🎯 Purpose of Responsive Design

  • To create one website that works on different screen sizes without the need to design multiple versions.

  • To ensure smooth browsing on all devices by avoiding unnecessary resizing, scrolling, or zooming.

  • To make websites more user-friendly and accessible.

⚙️ How It Works

  • A responsive website uses flexible layouts, grids, and CSS media queries.

  • The website scales up or down automatically to match the screen size of the device.

  • Example: The same webpage looks different on a desktop monitor compared to a mobile phone, but the content remains the same.

✅ Benefits

  1. Cost Effectiveness -  No need to build and maintain separate websites for different devices.

  2. Flexibility  -  Easy to adjust layouts and content for future devices and screen sizes.

  3. Improved User Experience - Visitors enjoy smooth navigation and readability, which increases engagement.

  4. Easy Management - Since only one website is maintained, updates and changes are simpler and faster.

👉 In short, Responsive Web Designing = One Website for All Devices.

title: Introduction to HTML
content:
HTML Basics

What is HTML?

HTML is an acronym which stands for Hyper Text Markup Language which is used for creating web pages and web applications. Let's see what is meant by Hypertext Markup Language, and Web page.

  • Hyper Text:  Hypertext simply means "Text within Text." A text has a link within it, is a hypertext. Whenever you click on a link which brings you to a new webpage, you have clicked on a hypertext. Hypertext is a way to link two or more web pages (HTML documents) with each other.
  • Markup language:  A markup language is a computer language that is used to apply layout and formatting conventions to a text document. Markup language makes text more interactive and dynamic. It can turn text into images, tables, links, etc.
  • Web Page:  A web page is a document which is commonly written in HTML and translated by a web browser. A web page can be identified by entering an URL. A Web page can be of the static or dynamic type. With the help of HTML only, we can create static web pages.

Hence, HTML is a markup language which is used for creating attractive web pages with the help of styling, and which looks in a nice format on a web browser. An HTML document is made of many HTML tags and each HTML tag contains different content.


 

Brief History of HTML

  • In the late 1980's , a physicist, Tim Berners-Lee who was a contractor at CERN, proposed a system for CERN researchers. In 1989, he wrote a memo proposing an internet based hypertext system.
  • Tim Berners-Lee is known as the father of HTML. The first available description of HTML was a document called "HTML Tags" proposed by Tim in late 1991. The latest version of HTML is HTML5, which we will learn later in this tutorial.

HTML Versions

  • HTML 1.0:  - 1991 (First version of HTML)
  • HTML 2.0:  - 1995 (support extra features such as form-based file upload, form elements such as text box, option button, etc.)
  • HTML 3.0: - 1997(capable of creating tables and providing support for extra options for form elements.)
  • HTML 4.01: - 1999(added support for stylesheets (CSS) and scripting ability for various multimedia elements.)
  • HTML5 : - 2008(initially) but stable updated version is October 28, 2014

Note - HTML5 is the newest version of Hyper Text  Markup language.

Features of HTML

  • It is a very easy and simple language. It can be easily understood and modified.
  • HTML is a case-insensitive language, which means we can use tags either in lower-case or upper-case
  • It is very easy to make an effective presentation with HTML because it has a lot of formatting tags.
  • It is a markup language, so it provides a flexible way to design web pages along with the text.
  • It facilitates programmers to add a link on the web pages (by html anchor tag), so it enhances the interest of browsing of the user.
  • It is platform-independent because it can be displayed on any platform like Windows, Linux, and Macintosh, etc.
  • It facilitates the programmer to add Graphics, Videos, and Sound to the web pages which makes it more attractive and interactive.

title: Block Of HTML
content:
Building blocks of HTML

An HTML document consist of its basic building blocks which are:

  1. HTML Tags:
  • An HTML tag are elements surrounded by angular brackets.
  • HTML tags are normally comes in the pair like <html> and </html>
  • The first tag in the pair is called start tag and second tag is called closed tag.
  • The Closed tag is written like a start tag but uses forword slash(/) before the tag name <html>--</html>,
    <head>--</head>, <h1>--</h1> ,etc.

 

  1. Attribute:
  • An attribute in HTML provides extra information about the element, and it is applied within the start tag. 
  • An HTML attribute contains two fields: name & value.
  • Ex- bgcolor, text, align,  width,  height,etc.
  • Syntax -
    <tag name attribute_name= " attr_value"> content </ tag name>
  • Example - <body bgcolor = “red” > ---------</body>

<html>

<head>

<title>The basic building blocks of HTML</title>

</head>

<body bgcolor = “red”>

<h2>The building blocks</h2>

<p>This is a paragraph tag</p>

</body>

</html>

What is Element ?

  • An element is the complete structure from the start tag to the end tag, including the content in between.
  • Element = Start Tag + Content + End Tag.

Types of Element

There are two types of element – 

  1. Container Element 
  2. Empty Element 
  1. Container Elements
    • Have a start tag, content, and an end tag.
    • Example:

<p>Hello World</p>

Here <p> is the start tag, Hello World is content, </p> is the end tag.

  1. Empty Elements
    • Only have a start tag, no content or end tag.
    • Example:

<br>   

<hr>

<img src="photo.jpg" >

Here <br> is the for line break ,<hr> for horizontal line and <img> is for image.

Note – The element are further classified by display in two categories 
  1.) Block element 

   2.) Inline Element  

( We Discuss  later)

title: HTML Page Structure
content:
Page Structure and Tags used in HTML

HTML consists of four major tags <HTML>, <Head>, <Title>,  <Body>.

  • <HTML> → It specifies the document as an HTML document.

  • <Head> → This tag contains information about the document, including its title, script, stylesheet, meta information, etc.

  • <Title> → This tag contains the document title.

    • The text written inside the <title> tag appears on the title bar of the browser’s window when the webpage is opened.

  • <Body> → This is the main tag of an HTML document.

    • It is the largest part of the HTML document.

    • The <body> tag includes all tags, attributes, and information to be displayed on the webpage.

Attributes of <Body> Tag

Attribute Description
bgcolor Changes the default background color to the specified color.
Example: <body bgcolor="skyblue">
text Changes the body text color to the specified color.
Example: <body text="red">
background Specifies the name of an image that will be used as the background of the document.
Example: <body background="sample.jpg">

 

 

 

 

 

 

Heading Tags

  • HTML has 6 levels of headings from <h1> to <h6>.

  • <h1> is the largest heading and <h6> is the smallest.

Syntax:

<h1>Heading 1</h1>

<h2>Heading 2</h2>

<h3>Heading 3</h3>

<h4>Heading 4</h4>

<h5>Heading 5</h5>

<h6>Heading 6</h6>

Break Tag(<br>)

  • Tag: <br>

  • Used when text needs to start from a new line and not continue on the same line.

  • Instead of leaving a blank line, we can insert a break tag.

Drawing Line (Horizontal Rule)

  • Tag: <hr>

  • Used for creating a horizontal line in HTML.

Attributes of <hr>:

Attribute Description Example
color Changes the color of the line <hr color="red">
width Sets the width of the line <hr width="60%">
align Aligns the line (left, right, center) <hr align="left">
size Changes the thickness of the line <hr size="5">

Paragraph Tag

  • Tag: <p>

  • This tag is used to break a paragraph and create a new paragraph.

Syntax:

<p>Paragraph content</p>

 

Align Attribute in Paragraph

  • The align attribute is used to align a paragraph to the left, center, or right in a document.

Example:

<p align="right">This paragraph is aligned to the right.</p>

title: HTML Formatting Tags
content:
HTML Formatting Tags 

नोट: - छात्र, इन सभी टैग्स का उपयोग करके कंप्यूटर पर HTML पेज बनाएं और जो आउटपुट आए उसे भी अपनी कॉपी में लिखें।

1. Bold Tag(<b>)

  • Displays text in bold (without importance).

  • Syntax:

    <b>content</b>

  • Example:

    <p>This is <b>bold text</b>.</p>

2. Italic Tag( <i>)

  • Displays text in italic style.

  • Syntax:

    <i>content</i>

  • Example:

    <p>This is <i>italic text</i>.</p>

3. Underline Tag( <u>)

  • Underlines the text.

  • Syntax:

    <u>content</u>

  • Example:

    <p>This is <u>underlined text</u>.</p>

4. Strike-through Tag (<strike>)

  • Shows text with a line through it.

  • Syntax:

    <strike>content</strike>

  • Example:

    <p>This is <strike>strike text</strike>.</p>

5. Big Tag(<big>)

  • Increases the font size of the text.

  • Syntax:

    <big>content</big>

  • Example:

    <p>This is <big>big text</big>.</p>

6. Small Tag( <small>)

  • Decreases the font size of the text.

  • Syntax:

    <small>content</small>

  • Example:

    <p>This is <small>small text</small>.</p>

7. Mark Tag(<mark>)

  • Highlights the text.

  • Syntax:

    <mark>content</mark>

  • Example:

    <p>This is <mark>highlighted text</mark>.</p>

8. Superscript Tag(<sup>)

  • Displays text slightly above normal text (useful for powers).

  • Syntax:

    <sup>content</sup>

  • Example:

    <p>2<sup>3</sup> = 8</p>

9. Subscript Tag(<sub>)

  • Displays text slightly below normal text (useful in formulas).

  • Syntax:

    <sub>content</sub>

  • Example:

    <p>H<sub>2</sub>O</p>

10. Quote Tag(<q>)

  • Defines a short quotation.

  • Syntax:

    <q>content</q>

  • Example:

    <p>He said, <q>HTML is fun.</q></p>

11. Blockquote Tag(<blockquote>)

  • Defines a long quotation (indented text).

  • Syntax:

    <blockquote>content</blockquote>

  • Example:

    <blockquote> HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language. </blockquote>

12. Deleted Text Tag(<del>)

  • Shows deleted text with a strikethrough.

  • Syntax:

    <del>content</del>

  • Example:

    <p>This is <del>wrong</del> correct.</p>

13. Teletype Tag(<tt>)

  • Displays text in monospaced (typewriter-style) font.

  • Syntax:

    <tt>content</tt>

  • Example:

    <p>This is <tt>teletype text</tt>.</p>

14. Preformatted Text Tag(<pre>)

  • Displays text exactly as written (preserves spaces and line breaks).

  • Syntax:

    <pre> Line 1 Line 2 (with spaces) Line 3 </pre>

  • Example:

    <pre> * HTML * CSS * JAVA </pre>

15. Abbreviation Tag(<abbr>)

  • Defines an abbreviation or acronym with a tooltip (using title attribute).

  • Syntax:

    <abbr title="HyperText Markup Language">HTML</abbr>

  • Example:

    <p><abbr title="Cascading Style Sheets">CSS</abbr> is used for styling.</p>

16. Font Tag in HTML (<font>)

  • The <font> tag in HTML is used to define the font size, color, and face for text.

Attribute Value Description
size 1 to 7 or relative (+1, -2)

Specifies the size of the text. Default is 3

<font size="4" >Hello World!</font>.
color Color name 

Sets the color of the text.

<font color="blue">Hello World!</font>
face Font family name (e.g., Arial)

Defines the font family for the text.

<font face="Arial" >Hello World!</font>

title: Main functions of computer system
content:
💻 Main Functions of a Computer System

All computer systems perform five basic operations to convert raw input data into meaningful information for users:

1. 🖱️ Inputting

  • The process of entering data and instructions into the computer system.

  • Examples: Keyboard, mouse, scanner, microphone.

2. 💾 Storing

  • Saving data and instructions so they are available for initial or future processing.

  • Storage can be temporary (RAM) or permanent (hard drive, SSD).

3. 🧮 Processing

  • Performing arithmetic or logical operations on data to convert it into meaningful information.

  • This is handled by the CPU (Central Processing Unit).

4. 🖥️ Outputting

  • Producing useful information or results for the user.

  • Examples: Printed reports, visual displays on monitors, audio output.

5. 🎛️ Controlling

  • Directing the manner and sequence in which all the above operations are performed.

  • Managed by the control unit within the CPU.

title: Components of a Computer System
content:
Components of a Computer System

A computer system consists of several essential components that work together to perform tasks efficiently. The main components include:

1. 🖱️ Input Unit

  • Accepts data and instructions from the user.

  • Converts them into a format understandable by the computer.

  • Sends the converted data and instructions to the system for processing.

2. 💾 Storage Unit

  • Provides space to store data and instructions.

  • Stores intermediate and final results.

  • Ensures data is available for current and future operations.

3. 🧮 Central Processing Unit (CPU)

  • Known as the brain of the computer.

  • Performs all major calculations and logical comparisons.

  • Controls and coordinates operations of other units.

🔹 Components of CPU:

Component Function
ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) Executes instructions, performs arithmetic (+, –, ×, ÷) and logical (<, >, =) operations.
CU (Control Unit) Directs operations of all other components, manages data flow, and acts as the “central nervous system” of the computer.

4. ⚙️ Processor (Microprocessor)

  • A single chip combining ALU and CU.

  • Often referred to as the heart of the computer system.

  • Determines the performance and speed of the PC.

  • Speed is measured in Million Instructions Per Second (MIPS).

5. 🖥️ Output Unit

  • Receives processed results from the computer.

  • Converts coded results into human-readable form.

  • Delivers the final output to the user or external devices.

title: Evaluation and history of computer
content:
History of computers

 

History of computer can be goes back to the beginning of human culture. People used simple objects like stones and pebbles for counting.

The Evolution of Computers:

The history of computers spans thousands of years, from early counting devices to the powerful systems we use today. 

  • The Abacus is known as the first device used for calculation around 600 BC. The modern form of the abacus appeared in the 16th century.
  • Napier's Bones was a manually-operated calculating device invented by John Napier(1550-1617) to simplify multiplication and division.
  • The first mechanical adding machine was invented by Blaise Pascal in 1642 (called Pascaline).
  • In 1671,Baron Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz invented the first calculator capable of performing arithmetic operations.
  • Charles Babbage, a 19th century professor of Cambridge university, is considered to be "Father of modern digital computer".
  1.   Babbage designed a difference engine in 1820 , which was used for calculation and printing of simple math tables.
  2.  In 1842 , Babbage design an analytical engine that was completely automatic. It was used for solving complex mathematical problems.

Some well-known early computer:

 Mark -1 :

  • Also known as automatic sequence controlled calculator, this was the first fully automatic calculating machine designed by

      Howard Aiken.
 ENAIC(1943-1946) [Electronic numeric integrator and calculator]:

  • It was the first electronic as well as digital computer designed by J.P Eckert and J. Mauchly.
  • It was developed as a result of military need.
  • It occupied a wall space of 20*40 square feet & used 18,000 Vacuum tubes.

 EDVAC (1946-1952)[Electronic discrete variable automatic calculator]:

  • It Was designed on stored-program concept .It was developed by John Von Neumann.

EDSAC(1947-1949)[Electronic delay storage automatic calculator]:

  • Almost simultaneously with EDVAC in the U.S., the British developed the EDSAC.
  • This machine was developed by a group of scientists headed by professor Mourice Wilkes .

 UNIVAC -1(1951)[Universal automatic computer]:

  • It was the first commercially available digital computer.

IBM 650/701[International Automatic computer]:

  • A commercially available digital computer that could be used for business and scientific

      calculations.

  • It was the first commercial computer that sold over thousands of computers.

title: Generation of computer
content:

Originally the term generation was used to differentiate between various hardware technologies.From the first electronic computer to the present computer, computer are divided into different generations for their classifications. Generation Period Hardware Software Examples
First 1942–1955 Vacuum tubes Machine language Mark-1, ENIAC, UNIVAC
Second 1955–1964 Transistors, magnetic tape Assembly language, batch processing OS Honeywell-400, IBM-7030
Third 1964–1975 ICs, semiconductor memory, magnetic tape & disk High-level languages (BASIC, COBOL, FORTRAN), parallel processing IBM 360/370, PDP-8/11, CDC-6600
Fourth 1975–1989 LSI, VLSI, microprocessors High-level languages (C, C++), GUI OS (MS-DOS, Windows) CRAY-1, Apple II
Fifth 1989–Present ULSI, AI technologies High-level languages (Java, HTML, CSS, Python), internet-based applications IBM notebooks, Pentium PCs, PARAM-1000, laptops, desktops

title: Input Devices
content:
Input devices

  • Input devices are used to input data and instructions into a computer system. 
  • An input device converts input data and instructions into a suitable binary form which is stored the primary memory of a computer.

Types of Input Device- 

Typing Device

Keyboard: 

  • The most widely used input device today is the keyboard. 
  • They allowed data entry into a computer system by pressing a set of Keys. 
  • The most popular keyboard used today is 101 to 108 keys.
  • Keyboard which is also known as Qwerty keyboard. 
  • Sir Christopher Latham Sholes invented the first Qwerty keyboard.
  • Keyboards are of Two types-
    • Standard Keyboard (General purpose keyboard) 
    • Multimedia keyboard (Special Purpose keyboard)
  • Types of Keys
    • Alphanumeric Keys— [A-Z],[a-z],[0-9]
    • Numeric Keyboard —The numeric Keyboard is a set of keys that looks like an adding machine with it 10 digit and mathematical Separator [ +, -, *, / ] 
    • Arrow keys — [up (↑), down (↓), right (→), left (←)]
    • Special function Keys — The Keyboard also has a set of special function keys,  Some important keys are –→ Enter Key, Backspace, Tab, Capslock, Numlock, Home, End, delete, page up, page down, insert space bar, print screen etc.
    • Function keys — there are 12 function keys in a keyboard. F1, F2, F3, F4 F5, F6, F7 F8, F9 F10. F11, F12 
    • Symbol Keys —  [<,>,+,-,*,-,!,#,@,&,%,$,\,/,{} 

Mouse :– 

  • It performs functions by detecting mouse dimensions motion.. 
  • It is held in one hand and moved across a flat surface. 
  • Generally it consists of two or three buttons on the top.
  • The mouse can also be used to control the computer system. 
  • It is also used to draw sketches, diagrams etc. 
  • Mouse was invented by Douglass Engelbart of Standard research centre in 1963.
  • Various technique that are used by mouse:- Operations performed by mouse-

1)pointing

2)Click, double click, triple click

3)left click (primary button), Right click (secondary button)(shortcut menu)

4.Scrolling

5.Drag and drop

6.Selection

  • There are two types of mouse:

I. Mechanical mouse(It uses rubber ball and sensor)

II. Optical mouse(It was light emitter and light detector or sensing based)

Trackball: It has a ball on its top which can be rolled by finger to move a graphics cursor around the screen.

Joystick: A joystick is a pointing device that looks like a car's gear and has a handle and a button on the top of the handle for controlling it is used to play games.

Light-pen or electric pen: It is a pen based system, you hold the pen in your hand and directly point with it  on the monitor or digitizer screen to select menu,icons,creating any image and canvas.

Touch screen: 

A touch screen enables us to choose from available options by simply touching with our finger on the desired icon or menu items, displayed on the screen.

Data scanning device:

Scanner: Data scanning devices are used for direct data entry into the computer system from the source document. A Scanner is a scanning device. It is a hardware device which is used to scan text or images into the computer system.

Type of scanner:

  1. Flatbed scanner [desktop scanner]
  2. Sheet bed scanner[roller fed scanner]
  3. handheld scanner [portable scanner]

OMR[Optical mark reader]: OMR are special scanners used for recognizing a pre-specified type of marks made by pencil or pen. It is used in various entrance examinations.

OCR[Optical characteristics reader]: This device is capable of detecting alphabetic and numeric characters on a computer print out containing a complete page of typed or handwritten text.

BCR[Bar code recognition ]: BCR are special devices used to read bar coded data. Bar code is a specialised code used for fast identification of items. It consists of small, dark and light strips called a bar.

 

MICR[Magnetic ink Character recognition]: MICR is used by the banking industry to facilitate the processing of cheques . MICR characters are printed in a special type face with a magnetic ink or toner usually containing iron oxide .

MICR code is made up of 9 characters.

Example: 201209202 →  201     209                202

                                 City name  Bank name    Branch name

Electronic or magnetic card reader: It is normally connected to a computer. It is used to read data encoded on the magnetic card and transfer it to a computer for further processing.

Digitizer: It is used for converting pictures, maps and drawing into a digital form for storage in computer. It is a tool used to convert hand-drawn images into a format suitable for computer

processing. It is also known as a graphics tablet.

Voice recognition system: This device allows a person to input data into a computer system by speaking to it.

Ex: Microphone.

Vision based: A vision based input system allows a computer to accept an input by seeing an object. Ex: web Camera

title: Image Tag
content:
Image Tag ( <img>) in HTML

  • An image can be inserted into a web page using the <img> tag.
  • The image tag takes the name of image with extension as an attribute (source).

👉 Syntax:

          <img src="image.jpg" >

Attribute of img Tag 

Attribute Value Description + Example
src URL / Path Specifies the source of image.
<img src="flower.jpg">
height Pixels (px) Specifies the height of the image.
<img src="flower.jpg" height="200px">
width Pixels (px) Specifies the width of the image.
<img src="flower.jpg" width="300px">
border Number (px) Specifies the width of border around an image.
<img src="flower.jpg" border="5">
hspace Pixels (px) Specifies the horizontal space (left & right) of the image.
<img src="flower.jpg" hspace="20px">
vspace Pixels (px) Specifies the vertical space (top & bottom) of the image.
<img src="flower.jpg" vspace="20px">
align left / right / center Specifies the alignment of the image.
<img src="flower.jpg" align="right">
alt Text Specifies the alternative text for an image (displayed if image is not loaded).
<img src="flower.jpg" alt="Beautiful Flower">

title: Marquee Tag
content:
Marquee Tag in HTML

  • The <marquee> tag in HTML is used to scroll text or images automatically across the screen, either horizontally or vertically.
  • It can be customized using attributes like direction, behavior, speed, and background color.

 

Attribute Value Description + Example
behavior scroll / slide / alternate Defines how text moves inside marquee.
<marquee behavior="scroll">Scrolling Text</marquee>
direction left / right / up / down Sets the direction of text movement.
<marquee direction="right">Moving Right</marquee>
scrollamount Number (px) Sets the speed of scrolling (in pixels per step).
<marquee scrollamount="10">Fast Scroll</marquee>
scrolldelay Number (ms) Sets delay between each scroll movement (in milliseconds).
<marquee scrolldelay="200px">Slow Scroll</marquee>
loop Number / infinite Defines how many times the marquee will repeat.
<marquee loop="3">Repeats 3 Times</marquee>
bgcolor Color name Sets the background color of marquee.
<marquee bgcolor="yellow">Yellow BG</marquee>
height Pixels (px) / % Specifies the height of marquee area.
<marquee height="100px">Tall Marquee</marquee>
width Pixels (px) / % Specifies the width of marquee area.
<marquee width="300px">Wide Marquee</marquee>

title: output devices
content:
Output device

  • An Output device is an electromechanical device which accepts data from the computer and translates them into a form which is suitable for use by the user. 
  • The result of any processing done by the computer to the outside world performed by the output devices.

Types of output:

I. Hard copy output: A hard copy output is produced on a paper. Ex: Printed paper by printer.

II. Soft copy output: A soft copy output is not produced on a paper. It is in magnetic form that

can not be used directly.

Ex: Monitor screen result.

 

Type of output devices

Monitor

  • Monitor is the most popular output device used today for producing soft copy
  • output. 
  • It is also called  Visual display unit(VDU).
  • The picture on a monitor is made up of thousands of small coloured dots called pixels.
  • There are two basic types of monitor:
    • CRT(cathode ray tube): A CRT monitor is similar to a television. 
    • It contains an electron gun at the back which fires electrons at the group of phosphorous dots ,as a result phosphorous dots glow and give the colours.
    • There are two types of CRT’s:
      • Monochrom
      • Colour
    • TFT (Thin film transistor): It is also called flat panel. It is of two types 
      • LCD(Liquid crystal display)
      • LED(Light emitting diode)

Projector: 

  • It is used for projecting information from a computer to a large screen so that it can be simultaneously viewed by a large group of people .
  • It is widely used for giving presentations.

Voice response system

  • A voice response system enables a computer to talk to the user.
  • It produces audio output. Ex: Speaker

Speech synthesizer

  • It is an output device that converts textual data into spoken sentences.

Hard copy device:

Plotter

  • It is an output device used to produce precise graphics under computer control. 
  • Plotters are ideal output devices for architecture, engineers and city planners.

Printer

  • Printer is the most popular output device. Commonly used for producing hard copy output .
  • Printer are Broadly classified into two categories:



 

  1. Impact printer
  1. Non-Impact printer
  • Dot matrix printer
  • Chain/band printer
  • Drum printer
  • Daisy wheel printer
  • Laser printer
  • Inkjet printer
  • Thermal printer


 

impact printer:

  • An impact printer uses an electromechanical mechanism that causes hammers or pins to strike against a ribbon and paper to print the text.
  • Impact printers can produce multiple copies of the text.
  •  The disadvantage of impact type printers is that they are noisy, lower print quality and slower than  non-impact printers.

Types of impact printer:

a) Daisy wheel printer:

  • It is a character printer.
  • It is similar to a type writer.
  • It uses a metal or plastic disc containing each of the letters, numbers and other characters it supports.
  • Speed 10-75 CPS (character per second).

b) Dot matrix printer:

• It is a character printer which prints one character at a time.

• It prints characters and all kinds of images as a pattern of dots.

• Use a pin as a hammer to print the text.

• Speed 30-600 CPS(character per second).

c)Drum printer:

• It is a line printer which prints one line at a time.

• It uses a cylindrical drum as its printing mechanism.

• Speed 300-2000LPM (line per minute).

d)Chain/band printer:

• It is a line printer which prints one line at a time.

• It consist of metallic chain on which all the characters of the character set are

embossed.

• Speed 150-2500 LPM (line per minute).

Non-impact printer: 

  • Non-impact printers do not use any electromechanical mechanism to strike against ribbon and paper. 
  • They use thermal, chemical, laser beam and inkjet technology for printing the text. 
  • Usually a non-impact type printer is faster than an impact printer. 
  • The disadvantage of non-impact type printers is that they produce only a single copy of text at a time.

Type of non -impact printer:

a)Inkjet printer:

• It is a character printer.

• It uses inkjet technology to print text.

• It uses liquid ink.

• Speed 40-300 CPS(character per second )

b)Laser printer:

• It is a page printer which prints one page at a time.

• Use laser beam technology for printing text.

• Usually it uses dry ink powder called toner.

• Speed 4-200 PPM (page per minute).

c)Thermal printer:

• It uses thermal technology.

• It uses a special heat sensitive paper.

• Speed -250 mm/s whereas 1 mm=8 dots.

title: HTML Links
content:
🔹 What are HTML Links?

  • Links are created in a webpage for moving across the pages or navigating from one page to another in a website.

  • Links are created using the anchor tag <a>.

  • Anything written between the anchor tag becomes a hyperlink.

Syntax:

      <a href="URL">Link Text</a>

👉 In the anchor tag, the most important attribute is href (Hypertext Reference) which specifies the URL of the webpage to be linked.

Example:

      <a href="https://www.google.com">Google</a>

Types of Links in HTML

There are two types of linking in HTML:

  1. External Link

    • Used to interconnect HTML webpages.

    • When you want to navigate to another page or any other URL, an external link is created.

    • This link may be an absolute path or a relative path.

    • Example:

      <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhagat_Singh">Bhagat Singh</a>

  2. Internal Link

  • A type of link that is used within the same page.
  • Useful in long pages with many subsections.
  • You can use the name attribute (or modern id attribute) in the anchor tag to identify a section, and then link to it.
  • Example:

                         <a name="section1"></a>

           <a href="#section1">Go to Section 1</a>

🔹 Link Colors

You can set the color of your links (unvisited, visited, and active) using link attributes inside the <body> tag.

  • Unvisited link → Blue and underlined (default).

  • Visited link → Purple and underlined (default).

  • Active link → Red and underlined (default).

Example (Changing Colors):

<html>
<head>
  <title>Link Colors</title>
</head>
<body link="green" vlink="yellow" alink="black">
  <a href="https://www.google.com">Google</a>
</body>
</html>

🔹 Image as Hyperlink

If you want to use an image as a hyperlink, the method is the same as with text links.

Example:

<body>
  <a href="https://www.google.com">
    <img src="logo.png" alt="Google Logo">
  </a>
</body>

title: Flowchart:
content:
Difinition: A flowchart is a visual representation of the steps or the flow of a process involved in solving a problem or performing a task. It uses a standardized set of symbols to depict the flow of control and operations within a system. Flowcharts are commonly used in programming, algorithm design, and process modelling to help understand and communicate complex processes in a clear, easy-to-follow manner.

Guidelines for Drawing a Flowchart

  • There should be only one entry/starting point and one exit point of the flowchart.
  • Use the correct symbol at each stage in the flowchart.
  • The logical flow should clearly be shown using arrows.
  • Use connectors to reduce the number of flow lines.
  • Lines should ideally be vertical or horizontal.
  • Do not give every detail on the flowchart. A reader who is interested in greater details can refer to the program itself.
  •  Statements in the flowchart symbols should be accurate  and easy to understand.
  • Be consistent in using names and variables in the flowchart. Use descriptive variable names.
  • Go from left to right and top-to-bottom while constructing flowcharts.
  • Keep the flowchart simple. The crossing of flow lines should be avoided.
  • If a new flowcharting page is needed, it is recommended that the flowchart is broken at an input or output point. Moreover, properly labelled connectors should be used to link the portions of the flowchart on different pages.

    Flowchart Symbols and Their Used:

    Symbol

    Symbol Name

    Use For

    Purpose

     

     Oval / Ellipse (Terminator)

     

    Start/Stop

    OR

    Begin/End

    Used at the beginning and end of the algorithm to show start and end of the program.

    Parallelogram

     

    Input/ Output

    Used for denoting program inputs and outputs.

                               OR

    Take values from an external source and assign them to Variables on a terminal or print the value of variables

    Rectangle (Process / Action)

    Processing  

    Indicates processes like mathematical and logical operations. OR Represents a process, operation, or action step

    Diamond

    Decision

    Represents a decision-making step (Yes/No or True/False) or Indicates a decision point

    Arrow

    Arrow or Flow Lines

    Shows relationships between different shapes.

                                   OR

    Shows the flow of the process from one step to another

       Circle

     

    On-page Connector

    Used to connect parts of the flowchart when space is limited or the chart spans multiple pages.

    Pentagon / Home Plate

    Off-page Connector

    Connects two parts of a flowchart which are spread over different pages.

title: Computer code
content:
Computer code


i. BCD code:

  • BCD stands for binary coded decimal.
  • BCD is a family of representation of numerals, upper case letters and some space special and control  characters.
  • It is designed by 6-bit of character and 64 characters can be coded.

ii. EBCDIC(Extended binary coded decimal interchange code):

  • It is 8-bit character set that was developed by IBM .
  • It was the character set used on most computer manufactured by IBM.
  • It uses 8-bit for each character or symbol and 256 possible characters can be coded.

iii. ASCII( American standard code for information interchange):

  • ASCII pronounced “askee” is the most common alpha numeric code used to represent characters, numbers and symbols.
  • ASCII code uses 7 or 8-bit for data representation. With 7-bit only 128 character can be coded and with 8-bit we can code 256 characters.
  • Characters include letters (A to Z, a to z), number (0-9),punctuation marks(!.,’ ‘ “), special characters (@ #$) and some control characters.

           EX: A=01000001
                 a= 01100001
iv. UNICODE:

  • UNICODE set of universal code it is an industry standard allowing computers to represent and manipulate text expressed in the most and the world writing system.
  • UNICODE provides a unique number, for every character.
  • Each character of symbol in UNICODE designed by a 32-bit number and the code can defined characters or symbols.
