title: Memory
content:
Memory

 

Memory–

  • Memory is an essential part of a digital computer .
  • It is a storage device that stores programs, data, information, results etc. 
  • The data and instructions that are entered into the computer must be stored into the computer system before starting actual processing .
  • Mainly memory are of two types:
    • primary memory
    • Secondary memory

 

1) Primary memory: Internal memory, main memory, temporary memory, Volatile memory.

 

2) Secondary memory: external memory, Auxiliary memory, Permanent memory, Non-volatile memory.

 

Units of memory: 

A computer stores and processes data or information in the form of binary numbers. The smallest unit of memory is a bit that can hold a single state either 0 or 1.

1 bit –→ 1 binary digit [0-1]

1Nibble –→ 4 bit

1Byte –→ 8 bit

1Kilobyte –→ 1024byte or 210 Byte

1Megabyte –→ 1024 KB or 220 Byte

1Gigabyte –→ 1024 MB or 230 Byte

1Terabyte –→ 1024 GB or 240 Byte

1Pentabyte –→ 1024 TB or 250 Byte

1Exabyte –→ 1024 PB or 260 Byte

1Zettabyte –→ 1024 EB or 270 Byte

1Yettabyte –→ 1024 ZB or 280 Byte

Concept of volatile and non volatile memory: 

Volatile memory:

Volatile memory is a type of computer memory that requires power to maintain the stored information. Once the power is turned off, all data is lost. 

Non-Volatile memory:

Non-volatile memory (NVM) is the type of computer memory that retains data even when the power is turned off. 

Note– In almost all computer systems the primary unit is volatile and the secondary unit is non -volatile Memory.

Primary memory: 

  • Primary memory holds only those data and instructions on which computer is currently working. 
  • It is generally made of semiconductors. 
  • A computer can not run without primary memory. 
  • Primary memories are of two types:

        1) RAM (Random access memory)

         2) ROM (Read only memory)

 

RAM(Random access memory):

• RAM is the read /write memory of a computer system.

• Information can be written into and read from a ram.

• It is a volatile memory that retains and stores information as it is supplied with power.

There are two types of RAM:

i. DRAM(Dynamic RAM)

ii. SRAM(Static RAM)

 DRAM: 

Dynamic RAM uses an internal circuit to refresh the storage every 2 milli second, It refreshes periodically.

Characteristics of Dynamic RAM:

• It has a very short data life.

• Need to be refreshed continuously.

• Slower as compared to SRAM.

• Large in size and Less expensive.

• Less power consumption.

SRAM:

A static RAM does not need any special regenerator circuit to retain the stored data.

The word static indicates that the memory retains its content as long as the power is being on.

Characteristics of static RAM:

• It has long life data.

• It is faster than DRAM.

• It needs not to refresh.

• Smaller in size and expensive.

• High power consumption.

ROM(Read only memory):

• ROM stands for read only memory.

• It is non-volatile memory which stores permanent programs that can not be altered.

• It stored a bulk of program where function is to start the computer, when power is turn on.

• Its contents are not lost when the power supply is switched off.

PROM :

  • It stands for Programmable Read Only Memory.
  • Its contents are designed by manufacturers. 
  • It stores permanent program function data and instructions.
  • once a data or program written in PROM, It can’t be erased.

2)EPROM(Erasable programmable ROM):

  1. UVEPROM(Ultra Violet Erasable programmable ROM): 

In this ROM programs are erased by using ultra violet rays and then reprogrammed.

The chip has to be removed from the computer erased using an UV rays emitting device.

  1. EEPROM( Electrically erasable PROM):
    1.  In this ROM the data can be erased by short circuit.
    2. It is easy to use because there is no need to remove the ROM from the motherboard.

Note: Booting: The process of starting up a computer system is called booting. 

1)Cold booting: when a computer starts for the first time it is called cold booting.

2)Warm booting: When the system restarts (shutting down and starting again or rebooting) is known as warm booting.

Secondary memory: 

  • Secondary memory is also known as external memory. 
  • This part of computer memory is non-volatile and has low cast per bit storage. 
  • It is used to store large amount of data on permanent basis which can be partially transferred to primary memory and when required for processing.

Types of secondary memory:

1) Sequential access memory:

Sequential Access Memory (SAM) is a type of memory or storage where data is accessed in a fixed, sequential order

magnetic tape: 

  • It is one of the oldest forms of secondary storage devices .
  • It is used as a backup storage. 
  • The magnetic tape is a plastic ribbon that is coated on one side with a magnetic material such as iron oxide.
  • Range: 1/4 inch 1/2 inch 50-240 feet long

2) Direct access memory: 

  • Direct Access Memory (DAM) refers to a type of memory or storage where data can be retrieved directly from any location, without the need to read through data sequentially. 
  • This allows for faster data retrieval compared to sequential access memory.
  • It has two types:

1) Magnetic disk:

  • A magnetic disk is a type of storage device that uses magnetic media to read and write data.
  • Magnetic disks are commonly used for storing large amounts of data and provide direct access to stored information.
  • It has two types:
  1. Floppy Disks:
  • A floppy disk is a round flat piece of flexible plastic coated with magnetic material .
  • It is encased in a square plastic jacket that gives holding protection to the disk surface .
  • Direct access but very slow compared to modern storage.
  • Floppy disk are available in two size:

Size (Diameter in inch) 

Capacity

5.25-inch

3.5-inch

1.2 MB

1.44 MB

 

  1. Hard disk: 
    1. A hard disk is a magnetic disk made up of metal and covered with a magnetic recording surface.
    2. It is the most popular medium for direct data access to secondary memory.
    3. Unlike floppy disks, hard disks are made of rigid metal (aluminium). 
    4. A single hard disk usually consists of several platters. 
    5. It is used to store huge amounts of data on a permanent basis. 
    6. There are two types of hard disk:

1) Internal hard disk

2) External hard disk

Components of hard disk:

1)Platter: the circular disk on which magnetic data is stored in a  hard drive is called a platter.

There can be several platters within the hard drive.

These platters are stacked and spin at high speeds.
2)Tracks: The surface of a disk is divided into a number of circles that is called track.

3)Sector : Each track is further subdivided into sectors.

4)Head: Each side of the platter is used to read/write data on disk.

5)Cluster: It is a group of sectors within a disk.

Access time: The data access time for a disk depends on three parameters:

1) Seek time : The time required to position the read/write head over the desired track is called seek time.

2)latency: The time required to spin (move) the desired sector under the head is called latency.

3)data transfer rate: The data transfer rate refers to the rate at which data is read from the disk.

 

2) Optical disk: 

  • The optical disk is a round disk made of Poly carbonate plastic
  •  on the surface of the optical disk is made of shiny with a thin layer of Aluminum to reflect light. 
  • An optical disk is a type of data storage medium that uses laser light to read and write data hence it is called a laser disk.
  • Optical disks are commonly used for storing large amounts of data, such as for music, movies, software, and backups.
  • type s of optical dick:
    • Compact disk 
    • Digital video disk 
  1. Compact disk:
  • It stands for compact disk.
  • CD’s  are circular disks that use optical rays, usually lasers, to read / write data.
  • A CD is a  round disk of polycarbonate plastic coated with a very thin reflective layer of Aluminium.
  • They are very cheap.
  • CD can explore up to 700mb of data.
  • CD’s are inserted in a CD drive built into the CPU cabinet. 
  • They are coatable as you can eject the drive, remove the CD and carry it with you.
  • Types of CD:
    • CD-ROM
    • CD-R
    • CD-RW
  1. CD-ROM:
  • CD-ROM stands for compact disk read only memory.
  • The dala in the CD-Rom is stored by the manufacturer in the factory itself which can not be changed later.
  • data can be read repeatedly from CD-Rom but new data can't be Stored (write)
  1. CD-R:
  • CD-R stands for compact disk Recodable.
  • It is a type of optical disk like a normal compact disk in which data can be stored by a computer with the help of a CD-R drive.
  • This is called a worm (write once, read many) Disk repeatedly.
    Data can't be changed once written.
  1. CD-RW:
  • CD-RW stands for compact disk Rewritable.
  • Data can be written and deleted on these optical disks again and again.

2. Digital video disk: 

  • It stands for digital video disk or Digital versatile disk.
  • It looks just like a CD and uses technology as that of CD’S
  • DVD Can Store 15 times the date held by CD's.  
  • A DVD holds 4.7 Mb to 17 GB of data.
  • DVDs achieve high storage capacity by using both sides of the disk, by using data comparison technology.

 

Mass storage device–

Mass storage device is referred to as the storage  device which can hold more data than normal storage device. 

USB Thumb Drive (Flash Drive)–

USB thumb drive normally known as flash drive or pen drive is used to store bulk data as per capacity. They are small in size with the USB face being portable to be used with any computer. 

Storage size: Small to medium (8 GB – 1 TB)

Use today: File transfer, backups, portability

High-speed flash memory storage

Lists in HTML are used to represent information in a structured format. They help in grouping related items together.

There are three types of lists in HTML:

  2. Ordered List (<ol>)

  3. Description List (<dl>)

🔹 Unordered List

An Unordered List user where sequencing not matter,it displays items with bullets (•) instead of numbers.
It is created using the <ul> tag with <li> for each item.

Syntax:

<ul>

  <li>Item Three</li>
</ul>

🔹 Ordered List

An Ordered List displays items in a specific order (numbered).
It is created using the <ol> tag, and each item inside it is wrapped in an <li> (list item) tag.

Syntax:

<ol>

</ol>

title: Memory bus
content:
Memory Bus

  • The memory bus is a communication pathway that connects the CPU (central processing unit) to the main memory (RAM) in a computer system. 
  • Physically, a bus is a set of wires which Carrys a group of bits in parallel. 
  • Every computer system has the following three types of buses for interconnecting the CPU and the memory.

Every computer system has three types of buses to connect the CPU and memory:

  1. Data bus
  2. Address bus
  3. Control Bus

1) Data Bus:

  • Transfer actual data between C.P.U. & Memory.

2)Address bus:

  • Carries the address (location) in memory where the CPU wants to read or write data.

3)Central Bus:

  • Sends control signals from the CPU to memory.
  • These signals tell memory whether to read data or write data at a paricular address.

title: Cache Memory and Register Memory
content:
Cache Memory

 

  • Cache memory is a  very small and very fast memory placed b/w CPU and main memory (RAM).                   
  • Cache is faster than main memory, so it improves the overall speed of the computer.                           
  • It works as a high-speed buffer b/w C.P.U. and main memory (RAM).
  • It is used to temporarily store very active data and instructions during processing. 
  • It stores frequently used data and instructions temporarily so the CPU can access them faster.
  • Access time of a cache memory is 15-25 nanosecond, while main memory takes about 25 nanoseconds.

  • Many Computer Systems are designed to have two Separate Cache memories- 

            1. Instruction Cache 

            2. Data cache

  • The instruction cache is used for storing program instructions and the data cache is used for Storing data.
  • Many computer systems are also designed to have multiple levels of caches such as- L1,L2,L3I

 

 

Register Memory

  • "Register memory" usually refers to a type of computer memory used in processors (CPUs). 
  • Register memory is a small, fastest type of memory used inside the CPU.
  • These registers are used to hold information on a temporary basis during instruction execution.
  • All the instructions are read and run by the CPU using these registers.
  • The size of registers is very small (measured in bits),but they work very quikly.

Common Types of Registers:

1)Memory Address Register (MAR): 

  1. It holds the address of active memory location.

2)Memory Buffer Register(MBR)/ MDR( Memory Data Register):

  • Temporarily holds data being transferred to or from memory.

3)Program Counter Register(PCR):

  • Holds the address of the next instruction to be executed.

4)Accumulator Register(ACC): 

  • Used in arithmetic and logic operations.

5)Instruction Register (IR):

  • Holds the current instruction that is being executed by the CPU.

6)Input/Output Register( I/O Register):

  • Temporarily holds data going to or coming from an I/O device.

7)Decoder: 

  • It has a necessary circuit way  to decode and interpret the meaning of each and every instruction supported by the CPU.

8)General Purpose Registers: 

  • Temporarily hold data during execution.

title: Introduction and History of Python
content:
Introduction : Python is a powerful high level, interpreted, interactive, general purpose programming language created by Guido Van Rossum in 1991 at CWI (Centrum wiskunde & Informatica) which is national Research institute for Mathematics and Computer Science in Netherlands and officially released on February 20, 1991. It uses English Keywords frequently whereas other languages use punctuations. Python Support both Procedural and Object Oriented Programming approaches.

  • Guido wanted to create a language that was:

    • Easy to read and write

    • Simple to learn

    • Powerful enough for real-world programming

    • Better suited for scripting and automation

  • Python was influenced by the ABC programming language, on which Guido had previously worked.

 

Why the name "Python"?

The name Python was not taken from the snake. Guido van Rossum was a fan of the British comedy television series Monty Python's Flying Circus. He chose the name "Python" because he wanted a programming-language name that was short, unique, and slightly humorous.

Python is used in various application areas such as the Web development, Gaming, Scientific and numeric computing, text processing and network programming etc.

Key Features of Python

  • Easy to Learn and Use – Python has a simple syntax similar to English.
  • Interpreted Language – Python code is executed line by line, making debugging easier.
  • Dynamically Typed – You don’t need to declare variable types explicitly.
  • Object-Oriented – Python supports procedure- oriented programming as well as object-oriented programming. In object-oriented languages, the program is built around objects which combine data and functionality.
  • Large Standard Library –One of Python’s best features is its large standard library that’s why it also described as “Batteries Included” Language.
  • Open-Source and Community: Python is open-source and its source code is available to the public for free. One great thing about Python is its large community that’s supportive and also always trying to improve it.
  • Platform-Independent – Works on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
  • Extensive Community Support – Has a vast community for help and resources.

HISTORY OF PYTHON:

  •  Python was developed by Guido van Rossum in the late eighties and early nineties at the National Research Institute for Mathematics and Computer Science in the Netherlands
  • There is a fact behind choosing the name Python. Guido van Rossum was reading the script of a popular BBC comedy series "Monty Python's Flying Circus". Van Rossum wanted to select a name which unique, sort, and little-bit mysterious. So he decided to select naming Python for their newly created programming language.
  • Python is derived from many other languages, including ABC, Modula-3, C, C++, Algol-68, Small-Talk, and UNIX shell, and other scripting languages. It is copyrighted. Similar to Perl, Python source code is now available under the GNU General Public License (GPL).
  • ABC programming language is said to be the predecessor of Python language
  • Python is General-purpose, Object Oriented, High-Level and Open Source Scripting Programming language.

Varieties of Python :

Because Python is Open Source, based upon programming Requirments happily we choose the corresponding version or we can customized and we can create our version or
flavors . Some are -

  • CPython : Work with C language
  • JPython : Work with Java Language with JVM
  • Anaconda Python : Work with large volume of data
  • Pypy : Python for speed compilation (JIT [Just in Time] Compiler.)

Technical Strengths of Python

Python is a powerful programming language with several technical advantages that make it suitable for various applications, from web development to  artificial intelligence. Below are its key technical strengths:

1. Simplicity & Readability:

  • Minimal Syntax – Python's syntax is clean and similar to English, making it easy to learn and write.
  • Whitespace Indentation – Uses indentation instead of brackets ({}), making code more readable.
  •  Dynamic Typing – No need to declare variable types explicitly.

 2. Portability & Platform Independence

  • Python is a cross-platform language, meaning it runs on Windows, Linux, macOS, and even embedded systems without modification.
  •  It supports Write Once, Run Anywhere (WORA).

3. Extensive Standard Library : Comes with built-in modules for various functions like file handling, networking, databases, and more.
Some key modules include:

  • math – Mathematical operations
  • os – Operating system interaction
  • sys – System-specific parameters
  • json – Working with JSON data
  • sqlite3 – Lightweight database

4. Memory Management

  • Python has automatic memory management using Garbage Collection (GC).
  • Uses Reference Counting & Cyclic Garbage Collector to free unused memory.
  • Developers don’t need to manually allocate or deallocate memory.

5. Multiparadigm Language

  • Supports multiple programming paradigms, making it highly flexible:
  • Procedural Programming (Using functions)
  • Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) (Using classes and objects)
  • Functional Programming (Using lambda functions and map/reduce)

6. Strong Support for Concurrency & Multithreading

  • Python supports multithreading and multiprocessing, allowing programs to run faster by executing tasks in parallel.
  • The threading and multiprocessing modules help with concurrency (homomorphism, likeness)

7. Strong Networking & Internet Protocol Support

  • Python has built-in support for handling HTTP, FTP, SMTP, and Socket Programming.
  • The requests module makes web scraping and API(Application Programming Interface)  handling easy.

8. Interoperability & Extensibility

  • Python can integrate with other languages like C, C++, Java, and .NET. It has bindings like:
  • Cython – To write C extensions
  • Jython – Python for Java
  • IronPython – Python for .NET

9. Robust Scientific & Machine Learning Support

  • Python is widely used in Data Science, AI, and Machine Learning because of libraries like:
  • NumPy – Numerical computing
  • Pandas – Data analysis
  • Matplotlib & Seaborn – Data visualization
  • Scikit-learn – Machine learning
  • TensorFlow & PyTorch – Deep learning

10. Secure & Reliable

  • Python has built-in security features that prevent buffer overflows, memory corruption, and injection attacks.
  •  Used in cybersecurity with tools like PyCrypto, Paramiko, and Scapy.

11.  Open Source & Community Support

  • Python is open-source and maintained by a huge community.
  • Regular updates improve performance and security.

Why Python?

✅ Easy to learn & use
✅ Highly portable & versatile
✅ Large standard library
✅ Excellent for AI, ML, and data science
✅ Strong community support

title: Introduction to Python Interpreter & Program Execution:
content:
Introduction to Python Interpreter and program execution

How Python Interpreter Works?

We have learned that Python is an interpreted language. Well, what does it mean? It means that we actually run another program that is responsible for reading our source code and running it Top To Bottom. In Python, this “another program” we just referred to iscalled an  Interpreter. Simply put, an Interpreter is a kind of program that executes other programs. Now, this interpreter itself can be implemented as a C program, or as a set of Java classes, or can be written in Python itself. The standard Python interpreter, though, is written in C, called the CPython.

  • Stage 1: Create and save a Python source code file (.py). Python Compiler begins reading the file.
  • Stage 2: Compiler converts the source code into platform- independent bytecode (.pyc) after checking for syntax and structural errors.
  • Stage 3: Bytecode is executed by the Python Virtual Machine (PVM), which translates it into machine code (binary).
  • Stage 4: Handling Errors (If Any)  If the program has errors, the Python interpreter stops execution and shows an error message. 
  • Stage 5: Machine code is executed by the CPU to produce the final output on the screen.


Method to install Python

  • Step – 1 - Download Installer: Go to the Python website (https://www.python.org/) , download the Python 3 installer for your OS.
  • Step – 2- Run Installer: Double-click to start installation.
  • Step – 3- Select Options: On Windows, check "Add Python to PATH" and choose "Install Now" or customize settings.
  • Step – 4- Finish Setup: Complete installation and close the installer.
  • Step – 5- Installation: Open a terminal, type python --version or python3 --version to confirm successful installation.
  • Step --6 - Verify pip installation by enter pip -v

After installation is successfully completed, you can start Python in the following ways These are:

(a) Python Shell – Interactive mode (Command line)

(b) Python Editor – Script mode (Integrated Development Environment – IDLE)

Interactive Mode (Python Shell)

Interactive mode of working means you type the command one at a time, and Python executes the given command and gives you output. An interactive interpreter of Python is also called Python Shell.

Click on Start Buttons--> Search Python ----> Press Enter

The Python interpreter can be used as a calculator. If you just want to do simple calculations, you can type numbers and operators and press Enter key to see the result, If you type 6+6, the interpreter displays result 12. You can Also Print statements Like Displaying “Hello World” in python type print (“Hello World”) and Press Enter.

Script Mode (Python Editor)
IDLE (Integrated Development and Learning Environment)

It is an integrated development environment (IDE) for Python. The Python installer for Windows contains the IDLE module by default. The interactive mode does not save commands entered by the user. But if you want to save all the commands in the form of a program file and see all output lines together then the script mode of Python is used. A program stored in a file (usually one that will be interpreted) is called a script. Python script mode is basically used for writing programs, i.e., a set of instructions that can be saved for further use.

title: Frameset tag in HTML
content:
HTML frameset Tag

The HTML <frameset> tag was used in older versions of HTML to create multi-pane layouts within a web page. By dividing the browser window into multiple sections, each frame could display a separate HTML document. This allowed for the creation of complex web layouts with different content in each pane.

Note: The <frameset> tag is deprecated in HTML5 and is no longer supported in modern web development.

Syntax

<frameset cols="pixels|%|*">
    <!-- Define frames here -->
</frameset>

 

Attributes used in Frameset

The list of frameset attributes is given below: 

🔹 <frame> Tag

  • The <frame> tag is used inside a <frameset> to define one frame (or section) of the browser window.

  • Each <frame> loads a separate HTML document within the same browser window.

<frame> Tag Attributes

  • src → URL of the document to load in the frame.

  • name → Assigns a name to the frame (useful for targeting links).

  • scrolling → Controls scrollbars (yes, no, auto).

  • noresize → Prevents resizing of the frame.

 

Example  - Create a HTML Page with 4 part part divided in frameset tag ..

Method 1 -

<html>
<head>
<title>Formatting</title>
</head>
<frameset cols = "50%,50%">
<frameset rows = "50%,50%">
<frame></frame>
<frame></frame>
</frameset>
<frameset rows= "50%,50%">
<frame></frame>
<frame></frame>
</frameset>
</frameset>

</html>

 

Method 2 -

<html>
<head>
<title>Formatting</title>
</head>
<frameset  cols = "50%,50%" rows ="50%,50%">
<frame></frame>
<frame></frame>
<frame></frame>

title: Style Menu
content:
Style Menu

About Style menu:The style options listed are typically used to apply predefined formatting to text, such as:

  • Paragraph formatting (like headings, lists, body text, and quotations).

  • Character formatting (like emphasis, strong emphasis, and source text).

The menu items shown fall into two main categories of styles: Paragraph Styles and Character Styles.

Paragraph Style:

These styles define the complete appearance of a paragraph, including aspects like text alignment, indentation, line spacing, font, and font size. They are applied to an entire paragraph.

Style Name Purpose
Title, Subtitle Used for the main titles and secondary titles of a document(Larger, often centered text).
Text Body(ctrl +0) The standard style for the main content or narrative of the document(Default font, size, and alignment).

Heading1(ctrl+1)

Heading2(ctrl+2)

Heading3(ctrl+3)

 Used to structure content into sections and subsections.
Quotations Used for longer extracts or quoted material(Often indented or with slightly smaller/italicized font).
Preformatted Text Used for text that should retain its exact spacing, like code(Monospaced font).
Bullet list, Number list Styles for various types of lists.

Character Styles:

These styles apply formatting to a selected word or phrase within a paragraph, without affecting the rest of the paragraph's overall format.

Style Name Purpose
Default Character Resets local character formatting(Normal text appearance).
Emphasis Highlights specific words for moderate importance(Usually Italics).
Strong Emphasis Highlights specific words for high importance(Usually Bold).
Source Text For marking up code, variable names, or technical terms within the body text(monospaced font).

Advanced Style Management:

The additional options relate to modifying or organizing the styles themselves:

Edit Style: Opens a dialog to modify the properties of an existing style.

Update Selected Style(ctrl+shift+F12): Updates the selected style to match the direct formatting of the currently selected paragraph.

New Style from Selection(shift+F12): Creates a new style based on the direct formatting of the selected text.

Load Styles: Imports styles from another document.

Manage Styles (F11): Opens the Styles pane for vast management of all document styles.

title: Hardware and software
content:
Hardware and software

Hardware:

  • The physical component of a computer system or pieces of equipment that is used to make up a computer system is known as computer hardware.
  • Peripheral devices: Peripheral devices are that which surround a computer system.

Ex: mouse, keyboard,monitor, CPU.

Software: 

  • Software is a set of instructions , programs or data  that tells a computer how to perform a specific task.or
  • Software is a collection of instructions, data or programs stored in a computer that tell the hardware what to do and how to do it.
  • Software directs the computer to perform the required Task.
  • It’s the non-physical part of a computer system, unlike hardware. 
  • Software can be broadly classified into two categories-
    • System software
    • Application Software

System software: System software sets of one or more programs that are basically designed to control the operation of a computer system.

System software control the following:

  • System software supports the execution of other application software and also supports the developments of other application software.
  • System software communicates with peripheral devices and controls the operation of peripheral devices such as printers, mouse etc.
  • Monitoring the use of various hardware resources such as CPU.
  • Examples:
    • Operating Systems (e.g., Windows, macOS, Linux)
    • Translator
    • Utilities (like antivirus, disk cleaners)

Application software: 

  • It is a set of one or more programs designed to solve a specific problem or do a specific task. 
  • Application Software is a set of programs, developed by programmers in order to perform specific tasks.
  • Application software in term talks with the system software for the execution.
  • Ex: Word processing software (e.g., Microsoft Word, libre office writer), spreadsheet software(e.g. excel,calc), Graphic software, Web browsers (e.g., Chrome, Firefox),Games, media players, etc.

Utility Software

  • Utility software is a type of system software designed to help analyze, maintain, optimize a computer system. 
  • utility software focuses on keeping the computer itself running smoothly.

Note– 

Bug: bug is a software error. Or

A bug is an error, flaw, or fault in a computer program.

Examples of Bugs: A calculator app Shows 2 + 2 =5,  A login form Accepts the wrong password, A website does not load images on mobile etc.

Debugging: Debugging is the process of finding and fixing bugs (errors or flaws) in a software program so that it works correctly. Or 

Making software bug free is called debugging.

 

Open source software or free software: 

Open source software is software whose source code is freely available for anyone to view, use, modify, and distribute. An open source software is free software.

 

Close source software or proprietary software:

Closed source software (also called proprietary software) is software whose source code  is not shared with the public, and the users are given only the compiled version , which they cannot legally modify, share, or distribute.

title: Form in HTML
content:
Form in HTML

What are HTML Forms?

Forms in HTML are used to collect input from users.
They allow interaction between the user and the website, such as login, registration, search, and feedback.

Forms are created using the <form> tag.

Basic Structure of Form

The main elements of a form are:

  • <form> → Defines the form.

  • <input> → Defines input fields.

  • <textarea> → Defines multi-line text input.

  • <select> → Defines a dropdown list.

  • <button> → Defines a clickable button.

Syntax:

<form>

Form Elements ..

</form>

1. The Input Element ( <input>) : - 

Input element is the most important form element that can displays in several ways depending on the type attribute for example if we using text field -

label  : <input type ="textbox">

Input element types 

 

 

🔹 Use of Radio Button

We use the radio button when we want to select only one option out of many choices.

Syntax:

Gender <br>
Male <input type="radio">
Female <input type="radio">


To link both "Male" and "Female" options together, we must use the same name attribute for both input elements. This ensures that only one option can be selected at a time.

Gender <br>
Male <input type="radio" name="gender">
Female <input type="radio" name="gender">
 

🔹 Use of Checkbox

We use the checkbox element when we want to select multiple options from the given choices.

Example:

Hobbies: <br>
<input type="checkbox"> Reading Books <br>
<input type="checkbox"> Cricket <br>
<input type="checkbox"> Playing <br>
 

If we want any option to be checked by default when the webpage loads, we use the checked attribute.

Example:

<input type="checkbox" checked> Reading Books

🔹 Textarea Tag

The <textarea> tag in HTML is used to create a multi-line text input field.
It allows the user to write more than one line of text, such as messages, comments, or feedback.

Syntax:

<textarea></textarea>

Note:
If you want to display a pre-filled (default) message inside the text box, you can write it between the opening and closing <textarea> tags.

Example:

 

<textarea>Enter your message here...</textarea>

 

🔹 Select Tag

The <select> tag in HTML is used to create a dropdown list.
It allows the user to choose one option (or multiple options if enabled) from a list.

Syntax:

 

<select>
  <option>Delhi</option>
  <option>Mumbai</option>
  <option>Kolkata</option>
</select>

Note:
If you want to display a default selected option in the dropdown, use the selected attribute inside the <option> tag.

Example:

<select name="fruit">
  <option selected>Apple</option>
  <option>Banana</option>
  <option>Cherry</option>
</select>

title: Programming language
content:
Programming language: 

  • A computer language is a means of communication used to communicate between user and computer.
  • With the help of computer language , a programmer tells a computer what he/she wants it to do.
  • All computer language can be broadly classified into the following three categories :
    • Low level programming language
      • Machine language
      • Assembly language
    • high level programming language

 

Low level programming language

 

1. Machine Language: 

  • There is only one language understood by the computer without using a translator program, this language is called machine language.
  • The machine language of a computer is normally written as streams or binary numbers(0,1).

Advantage of machine language:

1. Directly understood by the computer .

2. No translator of the program is required.

3. Programs executed very fast by the computer 

Disadvantage of machine language:

1. Machine dependency

2. Difficult to program

3. Difficult to modify

2. Assembly language: 

  • A language which allows instructions and storage location to be represented by letters and symbols instead of numbers is called an assembly language or symbolic language.
  • Introduction of assembly language in 1952 was the first step towards making programming tasks easier.

Advantage of assembly language:

• Easier to use.

• Easy to correct errors.

• Easy to modify

limitation of assembly languages:

• Machine dependent

• Need of translation

• machine level coding

 

High level programming language: 

High level programming language works designed to over complete limitations of low level programming languages (machine and assembly language ).

Advantage of high level languages:

• Machine independent

• Easy to use

• Easy to find errors

• Better documentation

• Easy to maintain.

Limitation of high level language:

• Need of translator i.e,compiler/interpreter .

• Execution time increases.

 

Some examples of High level programming language:

C++, Java, Python, PHP,FORTRAN, Cobol, Ruby,BASIC, PASCAL, logo, lisp, SQL etc.

FORTRAN–

Full form: (Formula Translation)

Developed by: IBM, led by John Backus

Released: 1957

Purpose: Scientific and engineering computations

COBOL–

Full form:Common Business-Oriented Language

Designed in: 1959

BASIC– 

Full form: Beginner’s All-purpose Symbolic Instruction Code

Designed in: 1964

PYTHON–

             Designed in: 1991

             Developed by:Guido van Rossum

C Language–

         Developed by: Dennis Ritchie at Bell Labs

 Released: 1972

Purpose: Used in developing application software and programs.

Translator is a program which is used to translate /convert assembly language/High level language into machine language.

title: Introduction To CSS
content:
Introduction to CSS

  • CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets.

  • It is used to format the layout of webpages.

  • CSS works with HTML and other markup languages to control how the content is presented.

  • CSS is a recommendation of the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C).

  • CSS is a stylesheet language used to describe the presentation of a webpage written in a markup language.

  • Using CSS, you can control:

    • Text color

    • Paragraph spacing

    • Font styles and sizes

    • Background color or background image

The concept of CSS is simple. First, the designer creates a standard HTML webpage. Then, using CSS, they define style rules (e.g., headings should appear in red and paragraphs in blue).

Advantages of CSS

  • Easy to manage

  • Saves time

  • Easy to maintain and update

  • Pages load faster

Example: 

<html>
<head>
  <title>CSS</title>
  <style>
    p { color: blue; }
    h1 { color: red; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <p>This is my first paragraph</p>
  <h1>This is my first heading</h1>
  <b>I am not affected by CSS</b>
</body>
</html>

In the above example:

  • h1 and p are selectors.

  • Properties such as color are declarations.

  • Values like red and blue are the values of those properties.

CSS Comments

  • Comments in CSS are written as:

                      /* This is a comment */

Syntax of CSS

The basic syntax is:

         Selector { Property: Value; }

Example:

      table { border: 2px solid red; }
         h1 { color: red; }

  • Selector: The HTML element you want to style

  • Property: The attribute you want to change

  • Value: The value assigned to the property

  • The whole line is called a declaration

 

Types of CSS

  1. Inline CSS

  2. Internal CSS

  3. External CSS

1. Inline CSS

  • Inline CSS is used to style a specific HTML element.

  • It is applied directly in the element’s style attribute.

  • Used when styles are needed only once.

  • Example

<html>
<head>
  <title>Inline CSS</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1 style="color: green;">Heading</h1>
  <p style="color: blue; font-size: 40px;">This is my first paragraph</p>
</body>
</html>

2. Internal CSS

  • Internal CSS is written inside the <style> element in the <head> section of the HTML document.

Example:

<html>
<head>
  <title>Internal CSS</title>
  <style>
    h1 { color: red; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Heading</h1>
</body>
</html>

4. External CSS

  • External CSS is written in a separate .css file.

  • It can be linked to multiple HTML files.

  • The file must have a .css extension.

Example:

<link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="style.css">

title: Introduction of Libre office Calc
content:
Introduction of libre office Calc 

Calc is the spreadsheet program of libre office. It is similar to programs such as Microsoft excel. It is alternative to Microsoft excel. 

Spreadsheet:

  • Spreadsheet is an application software.
  • A worksheet, also called a spreadsheet is an electronic sheet made up of rows and columns.
  • A spreadsheet is the place where the user works and performs arithmetical and functional calculations. 
  • By default it is named as sheet1,you can rename the sheet. 

 

Element of the spreadsheet: 

1)Row:

  • A row is a horizontal block of cells that spans the entire width of the spreadsheet.
  • A row is named as the no. Of 1,2,3...etc. In Calc total no. Of row is 10,48,576. 

First row - ctrl+

Last row-ctrl+ 

2) Column:

  • A column is vertical block of cells that spans the entire worksheet.
  • It is named as A,B,C...etc. In calc application, total number of column is 1024(AMj) or (XFD-16384 in new versions). 

First column-ctrl +

Last column-ctrl + 

3) Cell:

  • A cell is the intersection of rows & columns.
  • A cell in which mouse pointer is available that cell is known as active cells; cell may contain text, numbers and formulas. 

First cell name: A1 

Last cell name: AMJ 10,48,576 

4) Cell pointer or Mouse pointer: Boundary which highlights the cell. 

5) Cell address:<column name> <row name> 

Ex: A1 

 6) Cell range:  

  • A range is identified by it's first and last cell address, separated by a colon (:).
  • If you want to add cell A1 to A5 then we write formula =sum(A1:A5). 

Functions: A function is a predefined formula that performs calculation using specific values in a particular order. 

Exp: Sum(), power(), sqrt(), max(),count() etc. 

Formula:

  • In Calc, any formula is always starts by using equal sign.
  • A formula is an expression that operates on values in a range of cell or a cell.
  • It performs some operations like Mathematical calculations and logical operations and show on. 

Exp: A1 A2 A3 

        10  5  2 

      =A1+A2+A3 

Formula bar:

  • This bar appears at the right side of name box.
  • It displays formula as well as value entered into the active cell.
  • It also use to edit formula and content in it. 

Name box: The box appear at left of the formula bar and display the address of active cell. 

Active spreadsheet: The spreadsheet on which we are currently working.

Title bar: The name of the application file by default name untitled 1- libre office. 

Menu bar:

  • It is collection of commands or menus.
  • There are 11 menus in libre office Calc. 

[ File, Edit, View, Insert, format,Style, Sheet,Data, Tools, Window, Help] 

New sheet:

title: HTML 5.0
content:
Introduction to HTML5

  • HTML5 is the latest version of HTML (Hyper Text Markup Language).

  • It supports both HTML and XHTML syntax.

  • It introduces new elements, attributes, and behaviors.

  • It allows developers to create more powerful and dynamic web applications.

  • HTML5 includes a larger set of technologies that make web pages more interactive and multimedia-rich.

Features of HTML5

  1. New Semantic Elements:
    HTML5 introduces several new tags for better structure and meaning, such as:
    <header>, <footer>, <article>, <section>, <nav>, <figure>

  2. Improved Forms:

    • New input attributes (like email, url, date, placeholder, etc.)

    • Help create more user-friendly forms.

  3. Multimedia Support:

    • New tags for embedding media:
      <audio>, <video>, <canvas>, and <svg> (for graphics).

  4. Simplified Doctype Declaration:
          <!DOCTYPE html>

  5. Character Encoding Support:

                <meta charset="utf-8">

           It supports multiple languages and special characters.

 

Advantages of HTML5

  • Supported by all modern browsers.

  • Device friendly – works well on mobiles, tablets, and desktops.

  • Easy to use and implement.

  • Supports integration with CSS, JavaScript, and other scripting languages.

  • Helps in building beautiful, responsive, and interactive websites.

Disadvantages of HTML5

  • Only modern browsers fully support HTML5.

  • Writing long codes can be time-consuming.

  • Some features may not work properly in older browsers.

Basic Structure of an HTML5 Document

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>HTML5 Example</title>
</head>
<body>
  <header>Header content here</header>

  <nav>Navigation links here</nav>

  <article>
    <section>Section 1 content</section>
    <section>Section 2 content</section>
  </article>

  <aside>Sidebar or additional info here</aside>

  <footer>Footer content here</footer>
</body>
</html>

 

Explanation of New Tags

<header>

  • Defines the header section of a webpage or a section.

  • Commonly used for website titles, logos, or introductory information.

<nav>

  • Defines a navigation section containing links to other pages or sections.

  • Used for the main menu or navigation bar.

<article>

  • Represents an independent, self-contained piece of content, such as:

    • Blog posts

    • News articles

    • User comments

  • Multiple <article> elements can exist in one document.

<section>

  • Defines a specific section within an article or webpage.

  • Used to group related content together.

  • <article>
      <section>Section 1</section>
      <section>Section 2</section>
    </article>

<aside>

  • Used for sidebar content such as:

    • Additional information

    • Advertisements

    • Related links or notes

  • Can be placed left or right side using CSS properties like float.

<footer>

  • Defines the footer section of a document or article.

  • Commonly contains:

    • Copyright

    • Contact information

    • Navigation links

    • Social media links

title: HTML5 – <audio> and <video> Tags
content:
HTML5 – <audio> and <video> Tags

 

HTML5 introduced two important multimedia elements — <audio> and <video> — which allow developers to embed sound and video directly into web pages.
These tags make it easy to add, play, and control media files without using external plugins like Flash.

1. <audio> Tag

Purpose:

The <audio> tag is used to embed sound or music files such as songs, narrations, or effects on a webpage.

Basic Syntax:

<audio src="music.mp3" controls> </audio>

title: HTML5 – <iframe> Tag
content:
HTML5 – <iframe> Tag

Introduction

The <iframe> (Inline Frame) tag in HTML5 is used to embed another webpage or external content (like a video, map, or document) inside the current web page.
It creates a small window that displays the content from another source or URL.

Meaning

The term iframe stands for inline frame, which means a frame that is displayed inside the same page.

Basic Syntax

<iframe src="URL"></iframe>

Example

<iframe src="https://www.example.com"></iframe>

or 

<iframe src="index.html"></iframe>

or 

<iframe src="sample.jpg"></iframe>

Advantages of <iframe>

  • Allows embedding external websites, videos, or maps easily.

  • Keeps the main webpage independent from embedded content.

  • Can be used to display advertisements, forms, or other pages without reloading the main site.

Disadvantages of <iframe>

  • May cause slow loading if the embedded content is large.

  • Search engines may have difficulty indexing iframe content.

  • Not mobile-friendly if width and height are not responsive.

Attribute of <iframe> tag

title: CSS Selectors
content:
CSS Selectors

  • A CSS selector is used to select the content that you want to style.
  • It selects HTML elements based on their tag name, class, id, attribute, etc.
  • Selectors are an important part of every CSS rule set.

Types of CSS Selectors

  1. Element or Tag Selector

  2. Class Selector

  3. ID Selector

  4. Simple Selector

  5. Group Selector

  6. Universal Selector

  7. Combinator or Sub Selector

  8. Attribute Selector

1. Element or Tag Selector

The element selector selects HTML elements by their tag name.
For example, if you want to apply a style to all <p> elements, you can use the p selector.

Syntax:

p {
  text-align: center;
  color: red;
}
All <p> elements will appear with red color and center-aligned text.

2. ID Selector

The ID selector is used to style a specific element with a unique id attribute.
It is defined using a hash symbol (#) before the ID name.

Syntax:

#idname{

property: value;

}

Example:

<html>
<head>
<title>ID Selector</title>
<style>
#main {
  color: green;
  text-align: center;
}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<h1 id="main">This is a heading.</h1>
<p>This is a normal paragraph.</p>
</body>
</html>

 

 

Notes:

  • Each ID name must be unique in a page.

  • IDs are mostly used for specific, single elements.

 

3. Class Selector

The class selector is used to select elements that have a specific class attribute.
It is defined using a dot (.) before the class name.

Syntax:

.classname {

property: value;

}

<html>
<head>
<title>Class Selector</title>
<style>
.highlight {
  color: blue;
  font-size: 20px;
}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<p class="highlight">This paragraph is highlighted.</p>
<p>This paragraph is normal.</p>
</body>
</html>

 

4. Group Selector

The group selector is used to apply the same style to multiple elements at once.
You can group selectors by separating them with commas (,).

Syntax:

selector1, selector2, selector3 {
  property: value;
}
<html>
<head>
<title>Group Selector</title>
<style>
h1, h2, p {
  color: orange;
  text-align: center;
}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<h1>This is heading 1</h1>
<h2>This is heading 2</h2>
<p>This is a paragraph.</p>
</body>
</html>

5. Universal Selector

The universal selector applies styles to all elements in the HTML document.
It is represented by an asterisk (*).

Syntax:

* {

property: value;

}

Example :

<html>
<head>
<title>Universal Selector</title>
<style>
* {
  color: brown;
  font-family: Arial;
}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<h1>This is a heading</h1>
<p>This is a paragraph</p>
</body>
</html>

title: CSS Sub-Selector
content:
6. Combinator (Sub) Selector

  • Combinator selectors are used to select elements based on their relationship with other elements.
  • There are four main types of combinators:

1. Descendant Selector (space)

  • The Descendant Selector selects all elements inside another element, no matter how deep they are nested.

  • It uses a space ( ) between selectors.

Syntax:

div p {
  color: blue;
}
Example:

<div>
  <p>This paragraph is blue.</p>
  <section>
    <p>This paragraph is also blue.</p>
  </section>
</div>

 

2. Child Selector ( > )

  • The Child Selector selects direct child elements only of a specified element.

  • It does not select deeper nested elements.

Syntax:

div > p {
  color: red;
}

Example:

<div>
  <p>This paragraph is red (direct child).</p>
  <section>
    <p>This paragraph is not affected.</p>
  </section>
</div>

 

3. Adjacent Sibling Selector ( + )

  • The Adjacent Sibling Selector selects the first element immediately after another element.

  • Both elements must share the same parent.

Syntax:

h1 + p {
  color: green;
}

Example 

<h1>Heading</h1>
<p>This paragraph turns green.</p>
<p>This paragraph is not affected.</p>
<p>This paragraph is not affected.</p>
<p>This paragraph is not affected.</p>

 

4. General Sibling Selector ( ~ )

  • The General Sibling Selector selects all elements that are siblings of a specified element — not just the first one.

  • It also requires both elements to share the same parent.

Syntax:

h1 ~ p {
  color: purple;
}

Example:

<h1>Heading</h1>
<p>This paragraph is purple.</p>
<p>This one is also purple.</p>
<p>This another one is also purple.</p>

 

 

7. Attribute Selector

The attribute selector selects elements based on the presence or value of their attributes.

title: Python Character Set
content:
Python Character Set

A character set is a set of valid characters that a recognize (acceptable) by a programming language in scripting. Now, we are studying about the Python programming language. So, the Python character set is a valid set of characters recognized by the Python language and python follows the Unicode Character Set.
These are two type of character sets in python language. These are:

  1. Source Character
  2. Execution Characters/Escape Sequence

Source Character

  • Alphabets: All capital (A-Z) and small (a-z) alphabets.
  • Digits: All digits 0-9.
  • Special Symbols: Python supports all kind of special symbols like, ” ‘ l ;: ! ~ @ # $ % ^ ` & * ( ) _ + – = { } [ ] \ .
  • White Spaces: White spaces like tab space, blank space, newline, and carriage return.
  • Other: python can process all ASCII and Unicode characters as part of data or literals

Execution Characters/Escape Sequences:

Python allows to have certain non-graphic characters in string values. These characters are interpreted at the time of execution. Such characters cannot be typed directly from keyboard. e.g. backspace, tabs, carriage return etc. These can be represented by escape sequence. An escape sequence is represented by backslash followed by one or more characters.

Execution Character

Meaning

Result at Execution Time

\n

End of the Line

Move the active position to the initial position of the next line

\t

Horizontal Tab

Move the active position to the next horizontal tabulation position

\b

Backspace

Move the active position to the next previous position of the current line

\a

Alert

Produces an audible alert

\v

Vertical Tab

Move the active position to the next vertical tabulation position

\f

Form Feed

Move the active position to the initial position of the next logical page

\r

Carriage return

Move the active position to the initial position of the next paragraph

NOTE: Escape codes are embedded inside string literals and start with a backslash character(\)

title: Identifiers And Literals
content:
2. Identifiers

  • In a python program we have to use names to identify variable or to identify classes, methods/functions or modules , that names itself called as “Identifiers” which can be used for Identification.

  • They are essentially user-defined names and must follow certain rules to be valid.

Rules for identifiers:

  • It cannot start with a digit.
  • It consists of letters and digits in any order except that the first character must be a letter.
  • _ (underscore) can be used in identifier and underscore (_) counts as a character.
  • Spaces are not allowed. ·
  • Special Characters are not allowed. Such as @, #, $, %, + etc. in identifier
  • An identifier must not be a keyword of Python.
  • Variable names should be meaningful which easily depicts the logic
  • Commas or blank spaces are not allowed within an identifier

 

Testing the Validity of Python Identifiers:  The .isidentifier() function is used to check the validity of an identifier but, this method doesn’t take reserved keywords into consideration. So, we can use this function with keyword.iskeyword() to check if the name is valid or not.

  • print ("jai".isidentifier())                      Output:   True
  • print ("123jai".isidentifier())              Output:   False
  • print ("_jai".isidentifier())                     Output:   True
  • print ("for".isidentifier()  )                   Output:   True    # because for is keyword

 

3. Literals

 

  • Literals are the fixed values that are assigned to variables or constants.
  • These values are directly represented in the code and are of specific data types.

Type of Literal :

1. Numeric literals:

Numeric Literals are immutable. Numeric literals can belong to following four different numerical types.

  • Int (Signed Integers): Numbers ( can be both positive and negative) with no fractional part(decimal point). Ex: 100
  • Long (Long Integers): Integers of unlimited size followed by lowercase or uppercase L

Ex.: 87032845L

Note : - In Python 3, there is only the int data type for integers. The types long, short, signed, and unsigned were used in Python 2, but they are no longer supported in Python 3.

Float (Floating Point):  Also called floats, they represent real numbers and are written with a decimal point dividing the integer and fractional parts. Floats may also be in scientific notation, with E or e indicating the power of 10 (2.5e2 = 2.5 x 102 = 250).

Complex(complex): A complex literal in Python represents a complex number, which consists of a real part and an imaginary part.

Syntax :   complex_number = real_part + imaginary_partj

  • The real part is a float or integer.
  • The imaginary part is followed by j or J (Python uses j instead of i like in mathematics).

Examples:

c1 = 3 + 4j    # Complex number with real=3, imaginary=4

c2 = -5.2 - 2j # Complex number with real=-5.2, imaginary=-2

c3 = 0 + 1j    # Purely imaginary number

Program :

a = 2 + 3j

b = 1 - 4j

print(a + b)        # Output (3 - 1j)      Explanation :  (2+3j)+(1−4j)=(2+1)+(3−4) j       => 3−1j

print(a - b)        # Output (1 + 7j)      Explanation :   (2+3j)−(1−4j)=(2−1)+(3+4)j       => 1+7j

 

2.String Literals: 

String literals in Python represent sequences of characters enclosed in quotes. String literals are formed by enclosing text in the single or double or both a single and double (Triple) quote.

Example: String literals are a sequence of characters surrounded by quotes: single, double or triple.

                 Eg.: ‘John’, “Tom”, ‘Class 12’, “200453A”, ‘12345’

Single-line string: String created by enclosing text in single quotes, double quotes are normally single-line string, i.e., they must be terminated in one line.

Example: a=’John’

Example: text1= ’helloThere’

Multi-line string:  In multi-line string, text is spread across multiple lines as one single string. It can be created in 2 ways:

  1. By adding a backslash at the end of normal single quote or double quote string. In normal strings, just add a backslash before pressing ‘enter’ to continue.

             Example:  a=”nielit\

                                O LEVEL”  # do not indent when continuing typing in next line after’\’

  1. By typing the text in triple quotation marks.

              Example.  a=”””nielit

                              OLEVEL”””

                  b=’’’nielit

                             CCC’’’

# Single-line string

str1 = "John"

print(str1)

           # Multi-line string

str2 = """ This,

 is it!

"""

print(str2)

Size of String: Python determines the size of a string as the count of characters in the string.  e.g. size of  string “abc” is 3 and ‘hello’ is 5.

But, if our string literals have an escape sequence contained within it, then make sure to count the escape sequence as one character.

“abc”

Size is 3

 

 ‘\\’

Size is 1

\\ is escape sequence to represent backlash

“\ab”

Size is 2

\a is escape sequence, thus one character

“jai\’s pen

Size is 9

For typing apostrophe (‘) sign, escape sequence \’ has been used

“Amy’s”

Size is 4

Python allows a single quote (without escape sequence) in double-quoted string and vice-versa

 

For multi-line string with triple quote, while calculating the size, the EOL (End Of Line), the character at the end is also counted.

a=””” X    # enter keys are considered as EOL(End of Line) characters and counted in the length of multiline

 y

 z ”””      

Then size of string a is 5 (three characters x,y,z and two EOL character that follow character respectively But backslashes (\) at the end of intermediate lines are not counted in the size of the multiline strings.

 

 a=”c\

      d\

      e”

for multiline strings created with single/double quotes and backslash character at end of the line, while calculating size , the backslashes are not counted in the size of the string: also we cannot put EOLs using return key in single/double quoted multiline strings. so the size of string str is 3 (only three character no backslash counted)

Boolean Literals: Used to represent one of the two Boolean values, that is True and False .True is for 1   and False for 0.

For example:

>>>jai=(6>10)

>>>print (jai)

Output: False

4. Special Literals (None) :

The special literal  in Python represents the absence of a value or a null value. It is used to indicate that a variable exists but doesn't hold any meaningful data. It is commonly used in function definitions, default arguments, and as a placeholder when a value hasn't been assigned yet.

   5. Collection Literals :

Python provides four different types of literal collections:

  • List literals: [1, 2, 3]
  • Tuple literals: (1, 2, 3)
  • Dictionary literals: {“key”: “value”}
  • Set literals: {1, 2, 3}

Note - We will study collection literals in Chapter - 5( Sequence data types) in detail.

Constants

Python does not have built-in support for constants (like const or final in other languages). Instead, constants are defined by convention:
Variable names are written in UPPERCASE to indicate they should not be modified. Example:

>>> PI = 3.14159            # Ratio of circle circumference to diameter
>>> E = 2.71828             # Euler's number (base of natural logarithm)
>>> PHI = 1.61803           # Golden ratio
>>> SPEED_OF_LIGHT = 3e8    # Speed of light in vacuum (m/s)
>>> PLANCK_CONSTANT = 6.626e-34  # Planck's constant (J·s)
>>> AVOGADRO = 6.022e23     # Avogadro's number (particles per mole)
>>> BOLTZMANN = 1.38e-23    # Boltzmann constant (J/K)

 

It is up to the programmer to respect the constant nature of these variables.

title: Punctuators/ Comments/Data Types
content:
Punctuators

In Python, punctuators are symbols that help define the structure and syntax of the language. They are not used as operators, but rather to group, organize, or separate code. Here's a list of common punctuators in Python and their purposes:

  • : Colon: Used in defining functions, loops, classes, and conditional statements.
  • , Comma: Used to separate elements in lists, tuples, dictionaries, and function arguments.
  • . Period (Dot): Access attributes or methods of an object or module (e.g., object.method()).
  • () Parentheses: Used for function calls, grouping expressions, and creating tuples.
  • [] Square brackets: Used for list indexing, slicing, and comprehensions.
  • {} Curly braces: Used to define dictionaries and sets.
  • = Assignment operator: Assign values to variables.
  • -> Arrow: Used to indicate return types of functions (e.g., def func() -> int:).
  • ; Semicolon: Allows multiple statements on a single line, though its usage is rare in Python.

Python's punctuators help maintain its clean and readable syntax.

Expressions

  • It is any legal combination of symbols that represents a value.
  • An expression represents something, which python evaluates and which then produces a value
  • Example: 15, a+10, a+3, b>5

Statements

  • A statement is a programming instruction that does something i.e some action takes place 
  • Example: print (“hello Python”)

Comments in Python

  • A comment is a line of text in Python code that is ignored by the interpreter.
  •  It is used to explain code, document functionality, and increase readability.
  •  Comments do not affect the execution of the program.
  • Comments are the additional readable information, which is read by the programmers but ignored by Python interpreter
  • Add a # symbol in the beginning of every physical line part of the multiline comments

Types of Comments in Python :    Python supports two types of comments:

  1. Single-line comments
  2. Multi-line comments (or block comments)

1. Single-Line Comments

  • Single-line comments start with a # symbol.
  • The interpreter ignores everything after # on that line.

Example:    print("Hello, World!")  # This prints "Hello, World!"

2. Multi-Line Comments (Block Comments)

  • Python does not have built-in multi-line comment syntax like /* */ in C/C++.
  • However, you can use:
  • Multiple # symbols (preferred method) so Add a # symbol in the beginning of every physical line part of the multiline comments

Note: Comments enclosed in triple quotes (""") or triple apostrophe ('") are called docstrings.

A. Using Multiple # Symbols

#Multi-line comments are useful for detailed additional information.

# related to the program in question.

# It helps clarify certain important things.

B. Using Triple Quotes (""" """ or ''' ''')

  • Triple quotes are mainly used for docstrings.
  •  However, they can also be used for multi-line comments.

 “ “ “ Multi-line comments are useful for detailed additional

                                Information related to the program in question.

                                It helps clarify certain important things

“ “ “

NOTE :

    • Triple quotes (""" """ or ''' ''') are not ignored by the interpreter but stored as docstrings if they appear at the beginning of a function or class.
    • Comments enclosed in triple quotes (""") or triple apostrophe ('") are called docstrings

Python’s Built-in Data types : 

Python provides several built-in data types to store and manipulate different kinds of data efficiently. These data types can be categorized broadly into the following types:

1. Numeric Types

  • int: Represents integers (whole numbers). Example: x = 10
  • float: Represents floating-point numbers (decimal values). Example: y = 3.14
  • complex: Represents complex numbers with real and imaginary parts. Example: z = 2 + 3j

2. Sequence Types

  • str: A sequence of characters (text). Example: text = "Hello, Python"
  • list: An ordered, mutable sequence of items. Example: fruits = ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]
  • tuple: An ordered, immutable sequence of items. Example: coordinates = (10, 20, 30)
  • range: Represents a sequence of numbers. Example: nums = range(5) (produces numbers 0 to 4)

3. Set Types

  • set: An unordered collection of unique elements. Example: unique_items = {1, 2, 3}
  • frozenset: An immutable version of a set. Example: frozen = frozenset([1, 2, 3])

4. Mapping Type

  • dict: Represents key-value pairs. Example: person = {"name": "Naitik", "age": 25}

5. Boolean Type

  • bool: Represents logical values: True or False. Example: is_valid = True

6. Binary Types

  • bytes: Immutable sequence of bytes. Example: b = b"Hello"
  • bytearray: Mutable sequence of bytes. Example: ba = bytearray([65, 66, 67])
  • memoryview: A memory view object. Example: mv = memoryview(b"Hello")

7. None Type

  • NoneType: Represents the absence of a value. Example: value = None

title: CSS Background Property
content:
CSS Background Properties

The CSS background properties are used to define the background effects for an element.

There are five types of CSS background properties:

  1. background-color

  2. background-image

  3. background-repeat

  4. background-attachment

  5. background-position

1. background-color

The background-color property specifies the background color of an element.

Syntax:

<html>
<head>
<title>Background Color</title>
<style>
body {
  background-color: orange;
}
h1 {
  background-color: blue;
}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<h1>Heading 1</h1>
<p>Paragraph</p>
</body>
</html>

 

2. background-image

The background-image property is used to set an image as the background of an element.
You can also set the height and width of the background image.

Syntax:

<html>
<head>
<title>Background Image</title>
<style>
body {
  background-image: url('abc.jpg');
}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<h1>Heading 1</h1>
<p>Paragraph</p>
</body>
</html>

3. background-repeat

By default, the background image repeats both horizontally (x-axis) and vertically (y-axis).
The background-repeat property controls whether and how the image repeats.

Values:

  • no-repeat → The image will not repeat.

  • repeat-x → The image will repeat horizontally.

  • repeat-y → The image will repeat vertically.

  • repeat → The image will repeat both ways (default).

Syntax:

<html>
<head>
<title>Background Repeat</title>
<style>
body {
  background-image: url('abc.jpg');
  background-repeat: no-repeat;
}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<h1>Heading 1</h1>
<p>Paragraph</p>
</body>
</html>

4. background-attachment

The background-attachment property sets whether a background image scrolls with the page or stays fixed.

Values:

  • scroll → The background moves when the page scrolls. (default)

  • fixed → The background stays fixed when the page scrolls.

Syntax:

<html>
<head>
<title>Background Attachment</title>
<style>
body {
  background-image: url('abc.jpg');
  background-attachment: fixed;
}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<h1>Heading 1</h1>
<p>Paragraph</p>
</body>
</html>

 

5. background-position

The background-position property is used to control the position of the background image.
You can use keywords like left, right, top, bottom, or center.

Common Position Keywords:

  • left

  • right

  • top

  • bottom

  • center

  • left top
  • left bottom

  • right top

  • right bottom

  • center top

  • center bottom

Syntax:

<html>
<head>
<title>Background Position</title>
<style>
body {
  background-image: url('abc.jpg');
  background-repeat: no-repeat;
  background-position: center;
}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<h1>Heading 1</h1>
<p>Paragraph</p>
</body>
</html>

title: Operating System and functions of operating system
content:
Operating System

  • Operating system is a software program that controls internal activities of the computer hardware and provide user interface .
  • Application programs need to interact with the operating system for being hardware resources .
  • OS is the first program loaded in the memory after the computer is switched on. 
  • One of the primary functions of the o.s. is to provide an interface b/w the user and hardware .
  • This interface enables a user to use hardware resources efficiently.

 

Function of operating system:

1) Processor management: 

The operating system assigns a processor (If a computer has more than one processor) to the different tasks that must be performed by the computer.

2) memory management: 

OS allocates the main memory and secondary memory to the system program, user program and data.

3) File management: 

The O.S. is responsible for managing program files by default and also user files.

4) I/O management:

The OS is also responsible for all the input output devices such as mouse, keyboard, printer, web camera that are working properly or not.

5) Security management: 

OS stabilizes data security such that it keeps different programs and their data in such a manner that do not interface with each other. .It also protect data from being destroyed by any other user.

title: Types of Operating and User interface
content:
Types of OS:

1) Single user single tasking OS: 

The OS which allows only one user to work on a computer and can execute only a single task at a time is known as single user single tasking operating system.

Ex: MS DOS.

2) Single user multitasking OS: 

An operating system which allows only one user to work on a computer and can execute more than one task at a time is known as single user multitasking os.

Ex: Windows 95, windows98.

3) Multi user multitasking OS: 

This OS allows a number of users to work on a computer and can support the execution of more than one task at a time is known as multi user multitask OS.

Ex: Windows NT, Linux, Unix.

4) Batch OS: 

Sequence of jobs in a program on a computer without manual interventions.

Ex: Payroll.

5)Real time OS: 

Meant applications to fix the deadlines.

Ex: Robotics & Rocket launching.

title: MS DOS operating system
content:
Operating system for desktop and laptop :

MS DOS 

  • MS DOS stands for Microsoft disk operating system . 
  • It is a single user single tasking operating system. 
  • MS DOS was introduced in 1981. 
  • It was a joint project of IBM and Microsoft. 
  • It is a CUI ( character user interface) based OS. 
  • It is an OS with a command line interface used on personal computers.

How to open MS DOS:

1) Start →  All programs →  Accessories → Command.(For windows 7)

2) Windows + R →  Run → CMD → Enter.

Types of commands:

i. External command

ii. Internal commands

Internal commands: internal commands are commands which get loaded into the main memory of the pc at the time of booting or starting up of a computer.

Types of internal command:

1) cls (clear screen):

it means to change the directory .
