title: Windows operating system
content:
Windows operating system

  • MS Windows OS was developed by Microsoft  in1985 to overcome the limitation of its own MS DOS operating system.
  • The first latest released version of windows was windows 1.0.
  • The first successful version of this OS was Windows 3.0 which was released in 1998. 
  • The latest released version is Windows 11(2021). 
  • It is the world's largest selling OS for personal computers.
  • The main features of windows are:
  • It provides a GUI based user interface that  is so easy to work with.
  • It is a single user multi tasking operating system.
  • Run more than one program at a time.
  • Provide a way for you to manage files.
  • Provide a way for you to start an application program.
  • Windows comes with outlook express which is an Email program.
  • Ex: windows 7,windows 8 ,windows vista ,Windows 10.

Windows 10 desktop area: 

This is the main user interface of Windows 10 called desktop. It contains many icons and programs . These are:

Desktop: 

Desktop is a working area of windows , where you work is called desktop . As you work in windows you move items on the desktop .

Taskbar: 

  • The bottom dark portion is called the taskbar . 
  • It contains windows 10 start menu , cortana, search box, windows store ,documents, microsoft edge , battery life , sound, internet notifications and other icons.
  • It also helps you see the currently active or open windows program in your computer.

Start button: 

  • The start button provides access to the apps on your windows 10 pc and also to enhance the start menu. 
  • When you click on the start button , the start menu is displayed.

Search box/ cortana: 

  • The windows 10 search box is simple but there are ways to find things faster.
  • The search tool allows you to search specific types of items such as apps ,document , email , photos,
  • folder and so on.
  • Cortana helps you to find information , both on your computer and on the internet.

Notification area: 

The notification area appears on the right side of the taskbar. It shows different types of notification from your computer, like your internet connection , volume level and date/ time.

Icons and their types: 

An icon is a graphic object that shows a program or file on your desktop.

These are three types of icon:

1) System icons: 

System icons are displayed along the left edge of the screen . 

These objects are created automatically by windows during its installation. 

The five system icons are: 

  1. This PC( my computer)
  2. Control panel
  3. User’s file
  4. Network
  5. Recycle bin

2)Shortcut Icon: 

These are the icons with small arrows in the lower left corner. 

The shortcut icon provides easy access to some objects on your system, such as a program ,document or a picture.

* Deleting a shortcut icon does not delete the program from the hard disk.

 

3) program, Documents and folder icons: 

These are non-system icons without arrows and they represent the actual objects they describe.

* if you Delete such an icon you are deleting the object itself from the hard disk.

Essential windows accessories: 

Windows provides some utility software packages such as system tools, Entertainment, calculator, notepad, paint and word pad in the accessories group.

System tools: 

This option is found under accessories. It provides a set of tools for computer system management. It includes disk defragmenter, disk clean up etc.

Disk clean up: 

You can use disk clean up to free up space on your hard disk by removing temporary internet files, removing installed components and programs that you no longer use and emptying the recycle bin.

Start  →  All program  →  Accessories   →  system tool   →  disk clean up

Disk defragmenter: 

Disk defragmenter consolidates fragmented files and folders on your computer's hard disk, so that each file occupies a single, contiguous space on the volume. As a result, your system can gain access to your files and folders and save ones more efficiently.

title: Linux OS
content:
Linux operating system

  • Linux OS (Operating System) is a free and open-source operating system based on the Unix architecture.
  • Linux is a multi user multitasking operating system. 
  • Linux OS developed by Linus Benedict Torvalds in the year 1991. 
  • Linux is a 32 bit and 64 bit operating system. 
  • It runs on a wide variety of platforms such as Intel , Sparc ,Alpha etc.
  • Linux is distributed as a free software (open source) under a free software License.

Feature of Linux OS:

• Open source

• Secure

• Light weight

• Multi user & multitasking

• Application support for all

Basic components of Linux OS/ Basic Linux elements:

i. Kernel

ii. Shell

iii. File system

Kernel: 

  • The kernel is the core part of the Linux operating  system and is loaded into the memory as soon as the system starts up .
  • It manages main memory, files peripheral devices, maintaining the time and date, allocating system resources or functions of this part of the OS.
  • The kernel is a program at the heart of the linux OS.

Shell: 

Shell is a translator program which interprets(translate) commands given by the user.

File system:

  • Linux treats everything as a file .
  • All the hardware devices such as mouse ,keyboard ,hard disk also output devices are treated as a file. 
  • The linux file is organized in an hierarchy which starts with the root directory . 
  • The root is represented by a forward slash (/).
  • The file structure of linux are as follows:

/root


 

/root: It is the home directory for root user (admin).

/home: Home directory for root users(user create).

/bin: This directory contains commands used by all users including root user .

/sbin: This directory is used by only root users .

/dev: This directory contains device related files inside.

/etc: This directory contains a system configuration file in the form of a text file .

/lib: This directory contains library files, like a predefined function or method you use that shares its working definition from the library .

/tmp: This directory contains all the temporary files.

/user: This directory contains the home directory of the users. By default software installed in the directory.

/opt: Optional application software packages installed in this directory.(google chrome).

/mnt: This directory contains all the storage devices except the hard disk and mount them as well like CD-ROM, Floppy etc.

/kernel: This directory contains all the kernel specific code.

Linux commands: 

Linux commands are case sensitive . 

You must type all Linux commands in lowercase letters.

File handling in Linux: 

File handling in Linux OS systems is the subject matter of creating and manipulating the file as Linux provides GUI and CUI both the interfaces, here we will learn to work on commands in CUI . In CUI ,we are provided a $ prompt in MS DOS.

Files & directories in Linux OS:

Creating files( cat):

$cat> January press enter

Making new directories(mkdir):

mkdir sales enter

deleting files( rm):

$rm march enter

Moving files(mv):

$ mv rm enter

Removing to a different directory (cd):

$cd sales enter

Removing a directory (rmdir):

$ rmdir exam enter

Listing the contents of directories (ls):

$ ls enter

title: Ubuntu, Unix, MacOS OS
content:
Ubuntu Operating system

  • Ubuntu OS is a free, open-source operating system based on Linux. 
  • It is free of cost, available for individual community and professional use. 
  • Ubuntu is suitable for both desktop and server use. 
  • The ubuntu project is sponsored by canonical Ltd.
  • Canonical will not charge licence fees for ubuntu, now or at any stage in the future.
  • Ubuntu includes thousands of pieces of software, starting with the Linux kernel version4.15 and GNOME 3.28,and spreadsheet applications to internet access applications, web server software, email software, programming languages, different tools and several games. 

 

Method to download: 

To download ubuntu from the internet see the internet, see the download link below: Http://www.ubuntu.com/download

Unix

  • UNIX is a powerful, multiuser, multitasking operating system originally developed in the 1970s. 
  • It was first created at AT&T Bell Labs in 1969 by Ken Thompson, Dennis Ritchie, and others. 
  • It is proprietary software (close source).
  • The source code of Unix is not available for the general public. 
  • Unix primarily uses a command line interface. 
  • Unix is not portable. 
  • Unix is a rigid hardware environment.
  • Hence, can not be installed on every other machine. 
  • Unix is mainly used in server system, mainframes. 
  • Unix installation is comparatively costier than as it requires more specific hardware circuitry. 
  • Different versions of Unix are– AIS, HP, UX, BSD, Iris etc. 


 

Mac OS

  • Mac OS is a powerful, multitasking, graphical operating system developed by Apple Inc. 

  • It was first introduced in 1984 for Apple Macintosh computers.

  • It is a proprietary software (closed source) operating system.

  • It is UNIX-based, which makes it stable, secure, and efficient.

  • Mac OS is less portable, as it can only be installed and used on Apple hardware.

  • Mac OS is mainly used in personal computers, laptops, and professional creative systems such as video editing and design studios.

  • Its installation is costlier as it requires Apple’s specific hardware and licensed software.

  • Different versions of Mac OS include Mac OS X, OS X Lion, macOS Catalina, macOS Monterey, macOS Ventura, and macOS Sonoma.

title: Operating systems for mobile phone and tablets:
content:
Android OS

  • It was first released in 2008 and is primarily designed for smartphones, tablets, smart TVs, and wearable devices.
  • Android is an open-source operating system, based on the Linux kernel.
  • Android primarily uses a graphical user interface (GUI) with touchscreen support for user interaction.
  • It is a highly portable operating system, capable of running on various types of hardware from different manufacturers.
  • Android mobile OS have been developed Under “desert-inspired” version name with each new version arranged in alphabetical order with new enhancement and improvement.
  • Different versions of Android OS include cupcake, Donut, Froyo, eclair, Gingerbread, Honeycomb, ice cream, sandwich, Jelly bean, Kitkat, lollipop, Marshmallow, Nougat, Oreo, pie, Android 10(Sept,2019), Android 11 (2020), Android 12 (2021), Android 13 (2022), and Android 14 (2023).


 

iOS(iPhone operating system):

  • iOS is a powerful, multitasking, mobile operating system developed by Apple Inc.
  • It was first introduced in 2007 along with the first iPhone.
  • IOS is a proprietary software (closed source) operating system.
  • IOS primarily uses a graphical user interface (GUI) with touchscreen support for user interaction.

Blackberry OS

  • The source code of BlackBerry OS is not available to the general public.
  • BlackBerry OS is not portable, as it can only run on BlackBerry devices.

Windows OS for mobile

title: Cell referencing
content:
Cell referencing

Cell reference refers to the cell or range of cell in a spreadsheet. 

                                      OR 

A worksheet is created by rows and columns. Division of each row and column creates a cell, Each cell has a unique address. This address is called cell reference.The reference of a cell is following three types: 

  1. Relative Address 
  2. Absolute Address
  3. Mixed Address 

Relative Address:

  •  By default, all cell references are relative references.
  • When copied across multiple cells, they change based on the relative position of rows and columns.
  • For example, if you copy the formula = A1+B1 from row 1 to row 2, the formula will become =A2+B2.
  • Relative references are especially convenient whenever you need to repeat the same calculation across multiple rows or columns. 

Absolute Address: 

  • Absolute references do not change when copied or filled.
  • You can use an absolut It is used when you don't want a cell reference to change when copied to other cells.
  • Unlike relative reference to keep a row and/or column constant.
  • To create an absolute reference in a formula we add the dollar sign ($) before the column reference, the row reference or both. 

$A$2    The column and row do not change when copied

A$2           The row does not change

$A2           The column does not change

Mixed Cell reference: 

Mixed cell reference in Calc is a reference where both absolute and relative reference exists.

For example, the following references have both relative and absolute components:

=$A1 //column locked;A column locked but the row varies

=A$1 //row locked;Column A varies but row is fixed

=$A$1:A2 //first cell locked; but A2 can vary

title: CSS Border - Property
content:
CSS Border - Property


The CSS border properties are used to define the style, width, and color of the border around an element.
You can apply borders to almost any HTML element such as <div>, <p>, <h1>, etc.

There are three main border properties:

  1. border-style

  2. border-width

  3. border-color

You can also use the shorthand property border to set all of them together.

1. border-style

  • The border-style property specifies the type of line used for the border.

  • It must be defined first before color or width can be visible.

Syntax:

p {
  border-style: solid;
}

 

Common Values:

2. border-width

  • The border-width property defines how thick or thin the border should be.

  • You can specify the width in px, em, or named values like thin, medium, thick.

Syntax:

p {
  border-style: solid;
  border-width: 5px;
}

3. border-color

  • The border-color property specifies the color of the border.

  • You can use color names, hex codes, rgb(), or hsl() values.

Syntax:

p {
  border-style: solid;
  border-color: red;
}

 

🔹 Clockwise Rule (Common for Color, Style, and Width)

All three border properties —
border-color, border-style, and border-width — can take 1 to 4 values following the clockwise direction:

👉 Order:
top → right → bottom → left

Explanation-

🧾 CSS border-radius Property

The border-radius property is used to make the corners of an element rounded.
It defines the radius of the element’s corners.

🔹 Syntax:

h1{

border : 2px solid red;

border-radius: 2px;

}

title: CSS Box Model
content:
🧱 CSS Box Model

The CSS Box Model describes how every HTML element is represented as a rectangular box on a webpage.
It defines how margin, border, padding, and content work together to determine the total size of an element.

🔹 Structure of the Box Model:

Parts of Box Model 

 

🔹 Total Element Width & Height Formula:

Total Width  =  width  +  left padding  +  right padding  +  left border  +  right border  +  left margin  +  right margin
Total Height =  height +  top padding   +  bottom padding +  top border   +  bottom border +  top margin   +  bottom margin

🔹 Example:

div {
  width: 200px;
  height: 100px;
  padding: 10px;
  border: 5px solid black;
  margin: 20px;
}

here - 

Total Width = 200 + (10 + 10) + (5 + 5) + (20 + 20) = 270px
Total Height = 100 + (10 + 10) + (5 + 5) + (20 + 20) = 170px

title: CSS- List Property
content:
📝 CSS List Properties

 

CSS List Properties are used to control the appearance and style of lists (both ordered <ol> and unordered <ul> lists).
They define how the list markers (bullets or numbers) appear and how they are positioned relative to the text.

🔹 Types of CSS List Properties

Property Name

Description

Example

list-style-type

Specifies the type of marker used in a list

list-style-type: square;

list-style-position

Specifies the position of the list marker

list-style-position: inside;

list-style-image

Replaces the marker with a custom image

list-style-image: url('star.png');

list-style (shorthand)

Used to set all three properties in one line

list-style: square inside url('star.png');

🔹 1. List-style-type Property

It defines the shape or type of the bullet/number used for list items.

For Unordered Lists (<ul>)

Value

Description

Example

disc

Default filled circle

● Item

circle

Hollow circle

○ Item

square

Solid square

■ Item

none

Removes bullets

(no bullet)

 

For Ordered Lists (<ol>)

Value

Description

Example

decimal

Numbers (1, 2, 3...)

1. Item

lower-alpha

Lowercase letters (a, b, c...)

a. Item

upper-alpha

Uppercase letters (A, B, C...)

A. Item

lower-roman

Lowercase Roman numerals (i, ii, iii...)

i. Item

upper-roman

Uppercase Roman numerals (I, II, III...)

I. Item


 

Example:

 

ul {
  list-style-type: square;
}

ol {
  list-style-type: upper-roman;
}

🔹 2. list-style-position Property

Controls where the list marker appears — inside or outside the content area.

Value

Description

  

outside (default)

Marker is outside the text block. Text starts after marker.

  

inside

Marker is inside the text block. Text wraps under the marker.

  

Example : -

ul {

list-style-position: inside;

}

🔹 3. list-style-image Property

Allows you to use a custom image instead of a bullet.

Example:

ul {
  list-style-image: url('bullet.png');
}

🔹 4. list-style (Shorthand Property)

This property combines:

  • list-style-type

  • list-style-position

  • list-style-image

Syntax:

list-style: <type> <position> <image>;
 

Example :

ul {
  list-style: square inside url('bullet.png');
}

title: E-mail & E-mail protocols
content:
E-mail

  • E-mail Stands for electronic mail is one of the most widely used features of the internet.
  • Allows you to send and receive digital messages anywhere in the world.
  • It is based on client server architecture that provides a root, stored message service between any two email accounts.
  • Inventor: Ray Tomlinson, an American computer engineer
  • Year: 1971
     

Advantages of Email

  • Fast Communication
  • Cost-Effective
  • Easy to Use 
  • Environmentally Friendly
  • Accessibility
  • Can Send multiple copies

 

Disadvantages of Email

  • Spam and Junk Mail
  • Security Risks 
  • Requires Internet Access 
  • Hard to Convey emotions

E-mail Protocols

(i) SMTP(Simple Mail Transfer Protocol)

(ii) MIME (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions)

(iii) POP3 (Post Office Protocol version 3)

(iv) IMAP4 (Internet Message Access Protocol)

 

(i) SMTP(Simple Mail Transfer Protocol)

  • It is a push protocol.
  • It is used to upload mail directly from the client to the E-mail server of the user.
  • SMTP is a simple ASCII Protocol that uses TCP/IP networks.
  • Some older versions of SMTP can't handle message sizes   above 69 Kb.

(ii) MIME (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions)

  • It is also a push protocol.
  • This protocol is used for sending binary files or email attachment over the internet.
  • MIME allows an email message to contain a non- ASCII file such as an Image, audio, video, graphics etc.

(iii) POP3 (Post Office Protocol version 3)

  • It is a pull protocol that is used to receive and open email.
  • It deletes a message from the Server when a client reads the message.

(iv) IMAP4 - (Internet message Access Protocol)

  • It is a pull protocol that is used to receive and open email.
  • This protocol is designed to help users to need to use different types of computer in the office or at the home. 
  • This protocol gives interactivity to the user that a user can see (read) a message on the PC without deleting from the server.

title: Network
content:
Network

 

  • A computer is a collection of interconnected independent computers.
  • A network consists of two or more than two computers that are linked in order to share resources, information can be exchanged and allow communication.
  • The computer on a network may be connected through cable (wires) or without cable(wireless medium).

Advantage of computer network:

  • Data and program files can be shared.
  • Hardware resources can be shared.
  • Financial benefit.
  • Better communication medium.
  • Access to remote data.
  • Reliability

Types of network:

There are several types of networks-

  • Based on Area (size)
  • Based on Management method
  • Based on Topology (Network Structure)
  • Based on Connection Type

title: Network based on size
content:
Network based on size: 

Basically network is divided in to three parts according to size:

1. LAN

2. MAN

3. WAN

Local area network:

  • A group of networks is a computer network that interconnects computers within a limited area such as a school, Laboratory or office building.
  • It covers an area up to 5 km in diameter, but usually less than 1km.
  • A LAN is capable of accessing and sharing data devices in the LAN.
  • The speed of LAN’s network is 10Mbps to 100 Mbps or higher.
  • LAN supports a variety of communications transmission mediums such as Ethernet cable (thin cable, thick cable and twisted pair),fibre and wireless transmission.

Advantage of LAN:

  • Resource sharing (Printers, Scanners Modems, Hard disks can be shared within the connected devices).
  • This reduces cost and hardware purchase.
  • Easy and cheap communication
  • Centralized data
  • Internet sharing

Disadvantage of LAN:

  • High setup cost(Ethernet cable, switches, hubs)
  • Privacy violations
  • Data security
  • Covers limited area

Metropolitan area network:

  • A metropolitan area network is a network that interconnects users with computer, resources in a geographical area larger than that covered by LAN but smaller than the area covered by a WAN.
  • It covers an area between 5-50km in range.
  • MAN’s are formed by connecting multiple LAN's. 
  • Generally it is a network that  spreads over a city.

Advantages:

  • Less expensive
  • High speed than WAN
  • Conversion of LAN to MAN is easy.
  • High security

Disadvantage:

  • Difficult to manage
  • Hackers attack
  • Need more wires
  • Technical staff is required to set up.

Wide area network:

  • The network, which is spread over the globe and covers the entire world, is facilitated to a computer by Internet service providers.
  • It is the biggest network across the world in that each computer is connected and shares or accesses the data and information.
  • Through a wide area network, we can access the information stored away on the web server in seconds.
  • The only thing we need is to know the address of that data or information stored.

Advantage:

  • WAN covers a larger geographical area. Hence business offices situated at longer distances can easily communicate.
  • It allows sharing of resources.
  • It supports the global market and global business.
  • It uses advanced technologies.

Disadvantage:

  • Initial investment costs are higher
  • Difficult to maintain
  • Slow speed of data transfer
  • It has lower security compared to LAN and MAN due to wider coverage.
  • There are more errors and issues due to wide coverage.

title: Based on Management method
content:
Based on Management method:

Network architecture: 

  • Network technology means network layout that tells us how computers are arranged and how tasks are allocated to computers. 
  • It is also two types depending on the network management method:

i. Client-server architecture

ii. peer to peer (P2P) architecture

1. Client-server architecture: 

  • A network architecture in which each computer on a network is either client or server. 
  • Each device of the client can send data requests to one or more connected servers. 
  • In term the server can accept these requests ,process them and return the requested information to the client. Ex: www, Email

Advantage:

  • It has a centralized system, from which data can be easily backed up.
  • Security is better in this network.
  • The entire system is maintained by the server computer.

Disadvantage:

  • In case of server Failure the entire network will be failed.
  • Server maintenance cost is high.
  • It requires a dedicated network administrator to manage all the resources.

2. Peer to peer architecture:

  • Peer to peer is a type of network in which all the computers are directly linked together with equal capabilities and responsibilities for sharing data.
  • There is no special server in it.
  • Each computer manages its own Security.Ex: www, Email

Advantage:

  • It is a cheaper network as it has no server.
  • If one computer stops working it will have no effect on the other computer.

Disadvantage:

  • It has a security issue as the device is managed itself.
  • We can not backup the data because there is no server in this network.

title: E-mail Address & E-Mail structure
content:
E-mail Address– 

Every e-mail address has three main parts-

abc123@gmail.com 

  1.  Abc123 → Account name or user name 

All the email account names on a server have to be unique.

Email addresses are not case-sensitive. 

Account name cannot be longer than 64 character. 

  1. @ (at symbol) → 

Separates the username from the domain.There must be one (and ONLY one) @ sign in an email address. If the address does not have this sign —it is l'email address.

  1. gmail.com → Domain Name or name of server

This part of the email address is the name of the server that hosts your emails.

Structure of email

  •  Email Header Structure-

  1. From:
    The sender’s name and email address.
  2. To:
    The recipient’s email address(es).
  3. Cc (Carbon Copy):
    Other people who should receive a copy (visible to all recipients).
  4. Bcc (Blind Carbon Copy):
    Hidden recipients — others won’t see these addresses.
  5. Date:
    When the email was sent.
  6. Subject:
    A brief summary of the email’s topic (appears in the subject line).
  • Body – the main text or content of your email. Or  body contains the original message.
  • Attachment- 
    • E-mail has become more attractive to business because now it allows the user to attach a file to any email message.
    • any file format such as document images, audio or video files can be attached to an e-mail message. 
    • Attachment Size limit-

you can send up to 25 MB in attachments. If you have more than one attachment they can't  add up to more than 25MB.

  • Signature- 
    • The Signature of an email message is the personal information which automatically appears at the bottom of the outgoing message, use of signature is optional.
    • Signature block may include the following-
      • Full Name
      • Job title/Position
      • Organisation Name/division
      • Phone No. and E-Mail address.

title: Display property
content:
📝 CSS Display Property

The display property in CSS specifies how an element is displayed on the web page — that is, it determines the layout behavior of the element (how it appears and interacts with other elements).

Every HTML element has a default display value, which can be changed using CSS.

 

1. Block Example

<style>
div {
  display: block;
  background: lightblue;
  padding: 10px;
}
</style>

<div>This is a block element</div>
<div>This is another block element</div>

 

Output -  Each div starts on a new line.

2. Inline Example

 

<style>

  display: inline;
  width: 100px;
  height: 40px;
  background: orange;
}
</style>

<ul>

<li>Apple</li>

<li>Mango</li>

<li>Banana</li>

</ul>

3. Inline-Block Example

<style>

}

<ul>

<li>Apple</li>

<li>Banana</li>

4. None Example

<style>
p {
  display: none;
}
</style>

<p>This paragraph is hidden.</p>

title: User Input/Printing Statement/Block & Indentation
content:
Taking User Input in python

  • In Python for taking user input , we use  input() function.
  • When input() is called, the program pauses and waits for the user to type something and press Enter. 
  • After reading data, it converts it into a string and returns that.

NOTE: The input() method reads the user's input and returns it as a string.

  Syntax: input (prompt)

     Prompt (Optional) –A string that is displayed to the user (usually on screen)  before input.

Example 1: Write a program to Takes the user input using the input() method.

                      >>> name = input()            #  suppose we type How are you?

                      >>> name                               OUTPUT:   'How are you?'

Example 2: Write a program to receive a user's name using input method and print with Hello .

name = input("What is your name? ")

print("Hello,", name)

Above, the input() function takes the user's input in the next single line, so whatever user writes in a single line would be assign to a variable name. So, the value of a name would be whatever user has typed.

Example 3: Write a program to get the name using Input() with optional prompt parameter. Show them

>>> name = input('Enter Your Name: ')

       Enter Your Name: karamraji Institute

>>> name

OUTPUT:'karamraji Institute'

In the above example, the input('Enter Your Name: ') function with prompt string 'Enter Your Name: '. So, in the next line it will display a prompt first, asking user what to do. User can then enter the name after the prompt string in the same line and that would be assign to the name variable.

The input() function converts all the user input to a string even if that's the number.

Example 4:  Write a program to Get user's age and add 5 in the given Age

age = int (input ("Enter your age: "))

print("Next year, you will be", age + 5)

Example 5: Write a program to Add two numbers

num1 = int(input("Enter first number: "))

num2 = int(input("Enter second number: "))

sum = num1 + num2

print("The sum is:", sum)

Example 6: T Write a program to Take multiple inputs in one line

x, y = input("Enter two numbers separated by space: ").split()

print("You entered:", x, "and", y)    Output: You entered: 20 and 30

z=x+y

print(z)             Output:  2030

Example 7: Write a program to Convert input to float

price = float(input("Enter the price: "))

print("You entered:", price)

Output: Enter the price: 25.35

               You entered: 25.35

Example 8: Write a program to Convert input to int and print square

val = input("Enter an integer: ")  

val = int(val) # casting into string  

sqr = (val*val) # getting square  

print("Square of the value:",sqr)  

Output:  Enter an integer: 12

                Square of the value: 144

Printing statements in python 

          In Python, printing statements is straightforward, to the built-in print() function. It is used to display information, output results, or debug programs.

     Note: In Python, we use the print() function to display output on the screen.

 

Basic Syntax :    The print() function outputs text or variables to the console:

          Example :    print("Hello, World!")        # Prints a simple string

Printing Variables or multiple value :   You can use the print() function to display the value of variables:

Example:

name = "Naitik"

age = 25

class1=”10th “

print("Name:", name)

print("Age:", age)

print("class:", class1)

 or

            print("Name:", name, "Age:", age, "Class:", class1)

Using sep (Separator) in print() :

By default, Python separates values with a space, but you can change this using the sep parameter.

Example: print("Naitik", "25", "10th ", sep=" | ")

Output:  Naitik | 25 | 10th

Using end in print() :  

By default, print() adds a newline (\n) at the end. You can change this using the end parameter.

Example:

print("Hello", end=" ")

print("World!")

Output:  Hello World!

Printing Using String Formatting:

Python provides multiple ways to format output.

       (a) Using f-strings

Example :    name = "Naitik"

                                  age = 15

                                  print(f"My name is {name} and I am {age} years old.")

             Output: My name is Naitik and I am 15 years old.

        (b) Using format() Method

           print("My name is {} and I am {} years old.". format(name, age))

           Output:  My name is Naitik and I am 15 years old

       (c) Using % Operator (Old Method)

       print("My name is %s and I am %d years old." % (name, age))

             Output:   My name is Naitik and I am 15 years old

 

Block & Indentation

In Python, blocks and indentation are fundamental to its structure and syntax. Unlike many other programming languages that use curly braces {} or other symbols to define code blocks

Blocks: A block is a section of code that belongs together, such as the body of a function, a loop, a conditional statement, or a class.

Example:

if condition:

    # This is a block

    statement1

    statement2

Indentation:

  • Indentation is the leading whitespace (spaces or tabs) in a line that defines the level of the block.
  • All lines in the same block must be indented at the same level.
  • By convention, Python uses 4 spaces per indentation level, though using tabs is also allowed. Mixing spaces and tabs, however, leads to errors.

title: Introduction of Libre office impress
content:
Libre Office impress

Impress: Impress is the presentation (Slide show) program include in libre office.

                  

*Default Font name (Font Face) in impress: Liberation Sans

Extension of Libre office Impress: . odp

No. of menu available in Libre office impress:10

Deafult Orientation : Landscape

Impress window:

  • When you will open impress, a window will appears on your screen and you will find impress window in there parts of: Slide pane, workspace and side bar. 
  • You will see several toolbars create and format your text.
  • Slide pane contains thumbnail picture of slide in your presentation ,in the order the slides will be shown.

Slide Pane: 

  • It displays thumbnail pictures in your presentation in the order in which they will be shown unless you change the slide show order.
  • By using slide pane several addition operation can be performed as you can add new slides, Hide any slide,copy and paste, Move one slide to another place etc. 

Workplace:The workspace shown in middle of the with five view: Normal, outline, Notes,Handout and slide sorter.

Side bar: 

  • Sidebar normally open by default on the right sides of the impress window. you can select view > sidebox from the menu box to display it.
  • Sidebar containing eight sections as sidebar Setting,Properties,Animation, slide transition, Master slide ,Style, gallary and navigator, you can open only clicking on the icons.

Presentation: 

  • The presentation is a collection of individual slides that contain information on a topic.
  • For example educational purpose.

Slide:

  • Slide is a content page of Libre office impress which completes a pages to be printed along with notes pages. 
  • It is the place where you can type or insert the content about a presentation, colour it, assign a themes and style etc. to make the presentation attractive.

Title bar: 

  • This bar appears of the top of the documents & displays name of the file as well as minimize,restore, maximize and close buttons are available of the right side of this bar for controlling the window.
  • When the presentation is not yet named, you will see as:Untitled-1 Libreoffice impress

Note:  Alt +space +N- For Minimize window                   Alt +space +X- For Maximize window

           Alt +space +R- For restore                                   Alt + F4- Close window

Menu bar :  

  • A group of commands with 10 menus as File,Edit,View,Insert,Format Insert, format, Slide ,Slide show, Tools, window and help that allows the user to performs tasks.
  • It is located just below the title bar.

Toolbar:

  • The collection of buttons (usually with icons) that provide shortcuts to tasks typically located at the top of the screen. 
  • As you can see that Several toolbar can be used during creation of slide .
  • There are two visible standard toolbar and formatting which facilitate you to  make your presentation according to your requirement.
  • You can show or hide these toolbars by clicking view Menu> Toolbars.

Status bar: 

  • This bar appears of  the bottomof the screen that shows information about the document as page number, word and character count,page style, Language, selection mode etc.
  • You will see Information like current slide number and total pages ,view Layout and zoomslider with zoom percentage. 

View:

  • This menu provides several views in the presentation you can use and view and and demonstrate as well as.
  •  We have Normal view, slide shorter view, Notes ,pages view, Slide show view, slide Master view, Handouts master,Notes master view elc. 

Slide show: 

  • The continuous display of images, text our shapes with a certain transition or animation either sequentially shows or at random.
  • Slide shows created by stand alone by stand alone applications or a slide show function within a photo editor.
  • The internal between images is file to provide background music.

Placeholder:

  • In impress a placeholder is a box with a dotted outline, designed for the placement of content on the slide.
  • The placeholder is most commonly used for text.
  • You will see a prompt within the placeholder such as "Click to add text".

Design template:

  • A design template acts like a designer and decorator for the slides.
  • You use a number of theme templates and colors and controls to do it possible.
  • It is created so that even through different slide types can have different layouts and graphics, the whole presentation goes together a an attractive package.

* Creating a presentation using templates = shift + ctrl + N

Creation of presentation:

  • When you start libre office impress you will find a presentation wizard on your screen you can create empty presentation or designed templates according to your requirement.
  • Go to file menu> New >Templates or shortcut key(shift+ctrl+N)
  • A template dialog box will appear on screen, you can select one according to your choice and click open.

Creating a blank presentation:

  • Go to file menu> New> presentation or press(ctrl+N)
  • A template dialog box will appear on screen you can select templates of you want otherwise cancel template window.

To open an existing presentation:

  • Go to file menu> open or shortcut key (ctrl+O)
  • Select file location and file name then click on open button.

Inserting and editing text on slides:

1. While you create a new impress presentation, the first slide will appear.

2. To add text, click on the slide and start entering your text.

3. Any slide is the collection of objects (text, chart, picture, audio and video etc.)

There are following ways for inserting a slide in a presentation:

  •  You can add new slides by clicking new slide icon from standard toolbars.
  •  Go to slide menu > select new slide.
  •  Press ctrl+ M shortcut key.
  •  Select slide from the slide pane and press enter key.

Slide and slide Layouts:

♦ When you insert a new slide, it will usually have placeholders.

♦ Placeholders can contain different types of content, including text and images.

♦ Some placeholder have text which you can replace with your own text.

♦ Other have thumbnail icons that allow you to insert pictures, charts and

videos.

Slide Layouts:

  • Slide have different layouts for placeholder, depending on the type of information you want to include.
  • Whenever you create a new slide,you will need to choose a slide layout that fits your content.
  • When you open a blank presentation in libre office impress, the default layout called Title slide appears, but there are other standard layouts that you can apply.

* Number of layout is: 12

To add a text box(F2): Insert menu> Text box.

  • Text can be inserted into both placeholders and text boxes.

Inbox –

outbox–

outbox is the place where all the sent mails are stored until it is not fully sent. outbox gives the opportunity to the user review, edit and delete messages before they are sent.

Draft-

Junk–

Sent-

It is a place where all delivered mails are listed.

title: Designing Table using CSS
content:
Designing Tables through CSS

Tables can be styled beautifully using CSS to make them easier to read and visually appealing. Below are the main techniques used for table styling.

1. Adding Border to Table

Borders make the table cells and structure visible.
You can apply borders to the table, rows, and cells using the border property.

 

Syntax:

table,th,tr,td {

 border: 1px solid black; 

}

 

2. Border Collapse

When you add borders to both table and table cells, double borders appear.
To merge (collapse) them into a single border, use border-collapse.

 

Syntax:

table {
  border-collapse: collapse;
}

it have two values -

 

  • collapse → combines adjacent borders into a single line.

  • separate (default) → shows double borders between cells.

3. Making a Striped Table

Striped tables alternate row colors for better readability.

Syntax:

tr:nth-child(even) {
  background-color: lightgray;
}

  • nth-child(even) → targets even-numbered rows.

  • nth-child(odd) → targets odd-numbered rows.

 

4. Making a Hoverable Table

You can highlight a row when the mouse hovers over it using the :hover selector.

Syntax:

tr:hover {
  background-color: #ddd;
}

Question - Make a good looking table by using these above property.

title: Networking Devices
content:
Networking devices:

Node: 

Each and every device available on a network is called a node. Every node on a network has a unique MAC address.

Host: 

All the computers available on the network are called hosts. Hosts are also known as nodes.

Note: every host is a node, but not every node is a host.

Hub: 

  • Hub is a networking device for connecting multiple computers together and making them act as a single network. 
  • The hub broadcasts the signal to the computer to connect to it. 
  • It works at the physical layer of the OSI model.
  • Hub are of two type:

 

 

 

 

 

1) Active hub 

2) Passive hub

1) Active hub: It regenerates the faded signal and requires a power supply.

2) Passive hub: It does not regenerate the faded signal and does not require a power supply.

Switch: 

  • A switch also connects computers to teach others like a hub but a network switch forwards data only to one or multiple devices that need to receive it.
  • Switch establishes a direct connection between sender and receiver. 
  • It works on the data link layer of the OSI model.
  • It is also to be noted that a switch is a secure device because it sends information only to the desired destination.

Difference between hub and switch:

 

Features

hub 

Switch

Data transmission 

broadcast

According to need unicast,multicast,broadcast.

Duplex support

Half duplex

Full duplex

Security 

Secure Less 

More secure

OSI model 

Physical layer 

Data link layer

 

Bridge: 

  • A bridge is a network device that is used for connecting two LAN’s and allows computers to access resources. 
  • They can also be used to divide large networks into smaller segments.
  • Bridges are devices that can transmit data between two LAN’s. 
  • They also filter data and keep the traffic separate for each segment .
  • The bridge operates at both the physical layer and data link layer of the OSI model. 
  • It is full duplex.

Gateway: 

  • A gateway is a device used to connect dissimilar networks using different protocols.
  • It is also called protocol converter, that converts data packets from one format to another.
  • A gateway is necessary when there are different technologies implemented by the different networks which are to be connected together.
  • Ex: Network in New york and network in Delhi that are differ from each other.

Router: 

  • Routers are devices containing software that helps in determining the best path out of available paths for a particular transmission. 
  • It forwards data packets between networks.
  • Routers perform “Traffic directing “ functions on the internet. 
  • It works on the network layer of the OSI model.

Repeater: 

  • Repeaters are necessary since during the transmission of the signal over long distances. 
  • It is a network device which can boost up the weak signals. 
  • When the signal travels in the network after travelling some distance the intensity of the signal becomes low.
  • In order to regenerate the weak signal we should use a repeater device.

Modem: 

  • A modem is a networking device that allows you to connect and communicate with other computers via telephone lines. 
  • When digital signals are to be sent over telephone lines, it must be converted into analog form, this process is called modulation.
  • The reverse process, the conversion of analog signal into digital form is called demodulation.
  • The process of modulation and demodulation is carried out by a special device called modem.

title: W3-Color Classes
content:
W3-Color-Classes

 

In W3.CSS, colors are applied using simple predefined classes.
They make it easy to set background colors, text colors, and hover effects without writing custom CSS.

There are 4 main color-related class types in W3.CSS:

 

1. w3-color – Background Color

Used to apply a background color to an element.

Syntax:

<div class="w3-blue">This is a Blue Background</div>

 

2. w3-hover-color – Background Color on Hover

Used to change the background color when the user hovers the mouse over an element.

Syntax:


 

<div class="w3-hover-green w3-padding">Hover me to turn Green</div>

Example:

<button class="w3-button w3-red w3-hover-blue"> Hover to change Red → Blue </button>

 Note: You can use this class on buttons, divs, cards, menus, etc., to make interactive UIs.

3. w3-text-color – Text Color

Used to apply color only to text (not the background).

Syntax:

<p class="w3-text-red">This is red colored text</p>

4. w3-hover-text-color – Text Color on Hover

Used to change the text color when hovered.

Syntax:

<p class="w3-text-black w3-hover-text-red"> Hover over me to see red text </p>

title: CSS-Font-Property
content:
CSS Font Properties

CSS font properties are used to control the appearance, style, size, and typeface of text in HTML elements.
They allow you to make text attractive, readable, and consistent across your webpage.

1. font-family

Specifies the font type of the text.
You can list multiple fonts — if the first isn’t available, the browser uses the next.

Syntax:

font-family: monospace, Arial, sans-serif;

2. font-size

Defines the size of the text.
You can use absolute or relative units.

Common units:

  • px → pixels (fixed size)

  • em → relative to parent font size

  • % → relative to parent element

  • vw/vh → relative to viewport

Example:

p {
  font-size: 18px;
}
h1 {
  font-size: 2em; /* 2 times the parent size */
}

3. font-style

Sets the style of the font.

Values:

  • normal → Default

  • italic → Italic text

  • oblique → slanted text

Example:

p {
  font-style: italic;
}

 

 

4. font-weight

Sets how bold or light the text appears.

Values:

  • normal

  • bold

  • bolder

  • lighter

  • or numeric values (100–900)

 

Example:

h1 {
  font-weight: bold;
}
p {
  font-weight: 400;
}

 

5. font-variant

Used to display text in small-caps (capital letters with small uppercase size).

Example:

p {
  font-variant: small-caps;
}

 

6. font (Shorthand Property)

The font shorthand lets you define multiple font properties in one line.

Order of values:

font: font-style font-variant font-weight font-size/line-height font-family;

Example:

p {
  font: italic small-caps bold 20px/30px "Poppins", sans-serif;
}


Example (All Combined)

 

<style>
p {
  font-family: "Poppins", sans-serif;
  font-size: 18px;
  font-style: italic;
  font-weight: 600;
  font-variant: small-caps;
  letter-spacing: 1px;
  line-height: 1.8;
}
</style>

<p>This is an example of CSS font properties.</p>

title: Topology & types of Topologies
content:
Topology 

Network topology refers to the layout of a network, how different nodes are connected to each other and how the communication is stabilised in a network.

Types of topology:

1) Bus topology

2)Ring topology

3)Star topology

4)Mesh topology

5)Tree topology

6) Hybrid topology

1) Bus topology:- 

  • In Bus Topology every computer and network device is connected by a single length of a cable with a terminator at each end.
  • It is also called linear bus topology. 
  • It is passive topology which means only one  computer can send messages at a time.
  • The data signal is available to all computers that are connected in the network .
  • It carries the address of the destination computer and it is good for connecting 15 to 20 computers in a network.

 


Advantage of Bus Topology:-

  • Bus Topology is simple, reliable and best suited for small LAN.
  • Bus Topology required the less amount of Cable therefore less expensive.
  • It is easy to stand on a bus.
  • easy to connect or peripheral device to a Bus topology.

Disadvantages of Bus topology:-

  • If a wire breaks from any place, the entire Network is shut down. 
  • Heavy traffic can slow down a bus. 
  • collisions are the problem in the bus Topology.
  • There is a limit on central cable length and number of nodes that can be connected.
  • Security is very low because all the computers receive the sent signal from the source.

Ethernet:-

  • Ethernet was invented by Bob Metcalfe.
  • It was based on IEEE standard 802.3, CSMA/CD.

CSMA/CD:- 

  • In the term of networking, collision happens when two computers attempt to transmit data on the same wire at the same time, this creates a conflict .
  • The CSMA/CD protocol holds one data packet to prevent the collision . 
  • This is when only one data packet is transmitted at a time to prevent data collision.

Ring topology:-

  • In ring topology all the nodes are connected in a circular manner.
  • Data travel in around the ring in one direction.
  • It does not have terminated ends, data signals travel in a circle .
  • Ring networks typically use a token passing protocol.

 

Token ring:-

  • It is also called IEEE standard 802.5.
  • It is based on ring topology .
  • It has a free packet called a token that moves around the ring.
  • The computer that receives a free token can send its data.
  • This token gives equal chance to every node and moves to the next node after a fixed interval.

Advantage:-

  • Easy to install and maintain.
  • Every computer is given access to the token.
  • Reduce the chance of data collision.

Disadvantage:-

  • Failure of one computer on the ring affects the whole network.
  • Adding or removing devices to the networks disturb all other nodes.

FDDI ( Fiber distributed data interface) :- FDDI is another ring based network unlike token ring one transmitting data clockwise and another transmitting data anticlockwise.

Star topology:-

  • In star topology every computer is connected to a central hub or switch. 
  • It can be used with twisted pair, coaxial cable and fibre optic cable.
  • * In star topology for casting device hubs are not recommended because in hubs the data transmission is half duplex.

Advantage:-

  • A single computer failure does not break down the whole network.
  • It is easier to modify the network without disturbing it.
  • Easy to diagnose network fault.

Disadvantage:-

  • If the central hub fails its result is to fail the whole network.
  • Its cabling cost is high because each computer has its individual wire.

Mesh topology:-

  • In this topology, every node has a point to point connection to the other node.
  • All the computer systems interconnected to each other in a network.
  • It is fast , expensive and complex topology.

Advantage:

  • This network is very reliable.
  • If any link breaks, it will not affect the other connected computer .
  • It is very fast communication between the nodes.

Disadvantage:

  • This type of mesh topology is very expensive.
  • The installation process is difficult.

Tree Topology:-

  • It has a root node and all other nodes are connected to it. 
  • It is also called hierarchical topology. 
  • It should have at least three levels of hierarchy. 
  • It combined characteristics of bus and star topology.

Advantage:

  • It is easy to add a computer.
  • Fast expansion of nodes.
  • Easy to find errors.

Disadvantage:

  • Failure in the main bus cable will damage the overall network.
  • If any faults occur, it is difficult too.

Hybrid Topology:-

It is the combination of two or more topologies.

title: Conditional Statements
content:
Conditional Statements 

Conditional statements allow you to make decisions in your Python programs — like saying "if this happens, do that; otherwise, do something else."

OR

Conditional statements in Python allow the execution of different blocks of code based on specific conditions.

OR

Decision making is about deciding the order of execution of statements based on certain conditions.

Decision structures evaluate multiple expressions which produce TRUE or FALSE as outcome.

   Types of Conditional Statements:

There are basically 4 types of decision-making statements. Here is the list of all those four decisions making statements:

  1. if Statement
  2. if...else Statement
  3. elif OR if...elif...else Statement
  4. Nested if Statements

1. If Statement :- 

it Executes (should do something) a block of code if a specified condition is true. It First checks a condition — if it's True, it runs a block of code and If it's False, it skips that block.

Basic Syntax:

if condition:

    # code block that runs if condition is True

 

NOTE:

  • Always end the if line with a colon :.
  •  Always indent the code inside (usually 4 spaces).

Part

Meaning

if

Checks if a condition is True

: colon

Tells Python that a block starts

Indentation

Shows Python what code to run

 

 

 

 

Example:1

x = 10

if x > 5:

    print("x is greater than 5")

age = 18

if age >= 18:

    print("You are an adult")

2. If - else Statements :-

The if-else statement in Python allows a program to make a decision based on a condition.

It executes one block of code if the condition is true and another if the condition is false.

Syntax - 

if condition:

    # runs if True

else:

    # runs if False

title: Conditional Statements Part - 2
content:
3. If - elif - else Statements:-

The if-elif statement is a shortcut for chaining multiple if-else conditions. While using if-elif statement at the end else block is added which is performed if none of the above if-elif statement is true.

elif (else if) : elif stands for "else if" and is used in conditional statements to handle multiple conditions efficiently. It acts as an intermediate step between if and else, allowing Python to check additional conditions if the initial if statement evaluates to False.

Syntax:

if condition1:

         # Code block if condition1 is True

elif condition2:

          # Code block if condition2 is True

elif condition3:

        # Code block if condition3 is True

…..

…….

elif condition N:

        # Code block if conditionN is True

else:

         # Code block if none of the conditions are True

NOTE:

  • The if block is evaluated first.
  • The elif blocks are evaluated in order, only if the previous conditions were False.
  • The else block is optional and runs only if all previous conditions are False.

 

Example 1: Write a program to get the temperatures of City and print appropriate massage

                according the following-

      temperature greater 30 --à  it’s Hot outside

      temperature greater 20   --à  It's warm."

     temperature greater 10   --à It's  cool

                                         otherwise  --à print it’s cold

temp = int(input(“plz enter the temperature of your city”))

if temp > 30:

    print("It's hot outside.")

elif  temp > 20:

    print("It's warm.")

elif temp > 10:

    print("It's cool.")

else:

    print("It's cold.")

4. Nested if - else Statements

A nested if...else statement in Python is when you place one if...else block inside another. It's used to test multiple conditions in a hierarchical or dependent manner.

Syntax :

if condition1:

    if condition2:

        # code block if both condition1 and condition2 are True

    else:

        # code block if condition1 is True but condition2 is False

else:

    # code block if condition1 is False

When to Use:

  • When one condition logically depends on another.
  • To create multi-level decision trees.

Example:

x = 25 or x=int(input(“Plz enter the number”))

if x > 10:

    print("x is greater than 10")

    if x > 20:

        print("x is also greater than 20")

    else:

        print("x is greater than 10 but not more than 20")

else:

    print("x is 10 or less")

 

 

Example 1: Write a program to accept price and quantity of item from user and gives the discount as  per the following  slabs Structure:

  • 20% on amount exceeding 10000,
  • 10% for amount between 5000 To10000,
  • 5% if it is between 1000 To 5000.
  • no discount if amount<1000

quan=int(input("Plz enter the quantity of an items"))

price=int(input("Plz enter the price of an items"))

amount = quan*price

print('Amount = ',amount)

if amount > 10000:

   discount = amount * 20 / 100

else:

   if amount > 5000:

      discount = amount * 10 / 100

   else:

      if amount > 1000:

         discount = amount * 5 / 100

      else:

         discount = 0

print ('Payable amount = ', amount - discount)

Nested if statements:  An if statement inside another if.

                                                                                OR

A nested if statement in Python means placing one if statement inside another. It's used when you want to make a decision only after another condition is met.

 

Example:  Write a Python program that checks if a person is allowed to enter  to vote based on their age and whether they have a valid ID.

age = 20

v_id = True

if age >= 18:

    if v_id:

        print("You are allowed to enter.")

    else:

        print("You need a valid ID to enter.")

else:

    print("You must be at least 18 to enter.")

 

Example:  Write a Python program to evaluate a student's exam result and attendance status: If the score is 60 or higher, print "You passed the exam. "Then, check if the attendance is 75 or higher:

print "You also met the attendance requirement." If not, print "But you did not meet the attendance requirement." And If the score is less than 60, print "You failed the exam."

score = 85

attendance = 90

if score >= 60:

    print("You passed the exam.")

    if attendance >= 75:

        print("You also met the attendance requirement.")

    else:

        print("But you did not meet the attendance requirement.")

else:

    print("You failed the exam.")

Example:  Write a Python program that takes an integer input and do the following:

  1. Check if the number is positive.
  2. If it is positive, check whether it is even or odd.
  3. If it is even, further check whether it is greater than 10 or not.
  4. Print appropriate messages based on each condition.

num = 15

if num > 0:

    print("Positive number")

    if num % 2 == 0:

        print("Even number")

        if num > 10:

            print("Greater than 10")

        else:

            print("10 or less")

    else:

        print("Odd number")

else:

    print("Not a positive number")

 

 

Ternary Conditional Statements

A ternary conditional statement in Python is a shorthand way of writing an if-else condition in a single line.

Syntax:

          result = Statement1 if condition else Statement 2

Example:

age = 18

status = "Adult" if age >= 18 else "Minor"

print(status)                 # Output: Adult

 

Example:

x = 8

result = "x is even" if x % 2 == 0 else "x is odd"

print(result)

Example:

a = 5

b = 10

result = "a is smaller" if a < b else "b is smaller or equal"

print(result)

title: Transmission media
content:
Transmission media 

  • Transmission media is the way in which data is transmitted from one place to another place.
  • It provide a path way over which the message can trouble from Sender to receiver
  • Each of the messages can be sent in the form of data by converting them into binary digits.
  • These binary digits are then coded into a signal that can be transmitted over the app.

1. Guided (Wired) Media

  • In guided media, signals are transmitted through a physical path such as cables or wires.
  • The data signals are bounded into the cabling media therefore guided media is also called bounded media.

Types of Guided Media:

  1. Twisted Pair Cable
  2. Coaxial Cable
  3. Optical Fiber Cable

Different between Twisted Pair Cable, Coaxial Cable & Fiber Optic Cable

Feature

Twisted Pair Cable

Coaxial Cable

Fiber Optic Cable

Structure

Two insulated copper wires twisted around each other.

Central copper conductor, surrounded by insulation, metallic shield, and outer cover.

Core made of glass or plastic fibers that transmit light signals, surrounded by cladding and protective jacket.

Type of Signal

Electrical signals

Electrical signals

Light (optical) signals

Bandwidth / Data Rate

Up to 10 Gbps 

Up to 1 Gbps typically

10 Gbps to several Tbps

Transmission Distance

Up to 100 meters (Ethernet standards)

Up to a few kilometers

Up to 100+ kilometers without signal degradation

Noise / Interference

High susceptibility to EMI (Electromagnetic Interference)

Better noise resistance due to shielding

Immune to EMI and radio frequency interference

Installation & Handling

Easy to install, flexible

Moderate difficulty

Breakable and requires careful handling

Cost

Cheapest

Moderate

Expensive

Common Use

LANs, telephone lines, office networking

Cable TV, CCTV, broadband internet

Backbone networks, long-distance communication, high-speed internet

Security

Easy to tap/intercept

Moderate security

Very secure (hard to tap)

Examples / Types

UTP (Unshielded Twisted Pair), STP (Shielded Twisted Pair)

RG-6, RG-11

Single-mode fiber, Multi-mode fiber

Summary:

  • Twisted Pair: Cheap, flexible, best for short-distance LAN connections.
  • Coaxial Cable: Better shielding and higher bandwidth than twisted pair, used for broadband and TV.
  • Fiber Optic Cable: Best performance, highest speed, longest distance, and immunity to interference, but costly and delicate.

2. Unguided (Wireless) Media

In unguided media, signals are transmitted through air or space without physical cables.

Types of Unguided Media:

  1. Radio Waves
  2. Microwaves
  3. Infrared (IR)

Different between Radio Waves, Microwaves & Infrared (IR)

Feature

Radio Waves

Microwaves

Infrared Waves

Frequency Range

3 kHz – 300 GHz

300 MHz – 300 GHz

300 GHz – 430 THz

Wavelength Range

100 km – 1 mm

1 m – 1 mm

1 mm – 700 nm

Propagation

Can diffract, reflect, and penetrate buildings easily

Line-of-sight propagation (can be absorbed by rain)

Line-of-sight, easily absorbed by walls and obstacles

Speed

Speed of light (≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s)

Speed of light

Speed of light

Penetration Ability

Very high; can travel long distances

Moderate; limited by obstacles

Very low; absorbed by most materials

Data Transmission Rate

Low to medium

High

Very high (short range)

Typical Applications

AM/FM radio, TV broadcasting, mobile phones, Wi-Fi (lower bands)

Satellite communication, radar, microwave ovens, Wi-Fi (2.4/5 GHz)

Remote controls, thermal imaging, short-range sensors, fiber optic communication

Antenna Type

Long (dipole or monopole antennas)

Parabolic dishes, horn antennas

IR LED or laser diode emitters

Effect of Weather

Minimal

Affected by rain and humidity

Affected by fog, smoke, and obstacles
       
       

Summary:

  • Radio Waves: Best for long-distance and broad coverage communication (radio, TV, mobile).
  • Microwaves: Best for high-speed, medium-distance communication (satellites, radar, Wi-Fi).
  • Infrared Waves: Best for short-range, high-speed data transmission and sensing (remote controls, IR communication).

title: W3-Container or W3-Panel
content:
1.W3-Container Class

  • The w3-container class is a general-purpose layout wrapper that adds padding and helps structure your page content neatly.
  • It’s the most commonly used class in W3.CSS layouts.
  • It adds a 16px left and right padding to any HTML element.

  • The w3-container provides equality for all HTML container elements:

  • Common margins
  • Common paddings
  • Common alignments
  • Common fonts
  • Common colors

 

Syntax:

<div class="w3-container w3-light-grey">
    <h2>Welcome to Skilldotpy</h2> 
    <p>This is inside a W3 container.</p>
</div>

2.W3-Panel Class

  • The w3-panel class is used to create small, highlighted blocks of content (like notices, messages, or alerts).
  • The w3-panel class adds a 16px top and bottom margin and a 16px left and right padding to any HTML element.
  • It automatically adds margins around the element (unlike w3-container) and is ideal for standalone messages or info boxes.

Syntax- 

<div class="w3-panel w3-green">
  <p> Successfully Submitted!</p>
</div>

Example Comparing Both ( Only For lab work)

 

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://www.w3schools.com/w3css/4/w3.css">
</head>
<body class="w3-padding">

<h2 class="w3-center">Difference Between w3-container and w3-panel</h2>


<div class="w3-container w3-light-blue">
  <h3>W3-CONTAINER</h3>
  <p>This adds padding inside the box. Used for main content areas.</p>
</div>


<div class="w3-panel w3-pale-green w3-border w3-round">
  <h3>W3-PANEL</h3>
  <p>This adds margin outside the box. Used for alerts or notices.</p>
</div>

</body>
</html>

title: UPI, AEPS, USSD
content:
UPI:- [ Unified Payments Interface ] :-

  • UPI, which stands for Unified Payments Interface, is an instant real-time payment system developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) that allows users to instantly send and receive money between bank accounts using a mobile phone.
  • Perday transaction limit up to 1,00,000 (1 lakh) the transaction limit (24x7 and all public holidays)". 

Popular UPI Apps

  • Google Pay
  • PhonePe
  • Paytm
  • BHIM

Key Features of UPI

  • Instant money transfer (24×7, including holidays)
  • No need to enter bank account details every time
  • Uses a unique UPI ID (e.g., name@bank)
  • Supports person-to-person (P2P) and person-to-merchant (P2M) payments
  • Works directly with your bank account
  • Works with multiple banks in a single app
  • Secure with UPI PIN authentication

How UPI Works

  1. Link your bank account to a UPI app.
  2. Create a UPI ID (Virtual Payment Address).
  3. Set a UPI PIN.
  4. Send or receive money using:
  • Mobile number
  • UPI ID
  • QR code
  • Bank account details

 

 

 

 


 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

:Some Questino on UPI:

Q1. UPI was developed and operated by:    A) RBI   B) SEBI   C) NPCI    D) SBI

Q2. UPI is built on which banking system for fund transfers?   

                     A) RTGS only   B) NEFT only   C) IMPS   D) SWIFT

Q3.What is the full form of VPA in UPI?   A) Virtual Payment Address    B) Verified Payment Account   

                                                                    C) Virtual Personal Account   D) Verified Personal Address

Q4. Which organization regulates UPI in India?     

                       A) NPCI  B) Ministry of Finance  C) Reserve Bank of India (RBI)   D) NITI Aayog

Q5. Which feature allows a merchant to collect payment from a customer through UPI? 

               A) Push Transaction    B) Pull Transaction    C) RTGS Request   D) Electronic Clearing Service (ECS)

Q6. Which protocol enables interoperability among different banks on UPI? 

                 A) NPCI Switch     B) IMPS Infrastructure  C) UPI Switch   D) All of the Above

Q7. What is the primary purpose of a UPI Handle such as "user@bank"? 

      A) Encrypt transactions   B) Act as a Virtual Payment Address   C) Store transaction history   D) Generate OTPs

Q8. UPI supports which of the following transaction models?   

    A) Person-to-Person (P2P)        B) Person-to-Merchant (P2M)    C) Both P2P and P2M     D) Neither

Q9.. UPI Lite is primarily designed for:    A) International payments           B) High-value transactions 

                                                          C) Small-value transactions with faster processing      D) Corporate banking

Q10. Which of the following statements is TRUE?         

                A) UPI works only during banking hours      B) UPI requires sharing account details for every payment
              C) UPI enables real-time fund transfers 24×7             D) UPI can be used only on smartphones

ANSWERS:       Q1: C) NPCI              Q1: C) IMPS           Q3. A) Virtual Payment Address

AEPS [ Aadhaar Enabled Payment System]:- 

  • AEPS is a secure Payment platform for financial transactions based on a unique identification number that enables a user for the cashless transaction. 
  • This system was developed by NPCI [National Payment Corporation of India] and released on 28 Aug 2014. 
  • It allows the user to perform banking transactions like balance inquiry, cash deposit, cash withdrawal etc.

title: Introduction to internet & www
content:
Internet

  • The Internet is an interconnection between severed computers of different types belonging to various networks across the world.
  • “It is a network of networks” Million of people use the internet to search and share information and ideas etc.
  • The computers on the internet communicate with each other using the Transmission Control Protocol/ Internet Protocol (TCP/IP).
  • Father of the internet is Vint Cerf.
  •  The first internet  started as a United State America(USA) government project in the  year 1969 called the ARPANET (Advanced research Projects Agency network) built by a division of the Department of Defense.
  • In the late 70's the NSFNET, the National Science Foundation Network was developed.
  • The First publicly available internet Service in India was launched by State-owned  Videsh Sanchar Nigam Limited (VSNL) on  15 August 1995.

Basic Characteristics of internet: `

1)Decentralised

2) Easy for communication

3)It offers information 24 hours a day.

4) There is no limit to the number of users that can be added to it.

5) It has no geographical limitations.

Element of Internet: A simplified model of the internet is:

Client’s PC’s

Server computer

Networking

Client PC’s: There are the computers that request from servers and it required part time

maintenance.

Server computer: A server is a computer that holds files or websites. These are powerful

computers and can provide data to multiple client computers simultaneously.

Networks: These are composed of one or more servers and multiple client PC’s.

Application of internet:

• Online transaction

• Searching

• Online ticketing

• E- commerce

• Weather forecasting

• e-commerce

 

Introduction to WWW

  • World wide web, which is also known as a Web, is the part of the internet that contains websites and web pages.
  • WWW is a collection of web pages interconnected through hypertext which are stored in web servers and connected to local computers through the internet.
  • WWW works on Client-Server Architecture, in WWW documents written in HTML language.
  • WWW  was developed by Tim Berners Lee in (1989) Geneva Switzerland.

Note– First web browser is Mosaic (1992). Netscape Navigator(1994)

Elements of www

  • Website
  • Webpage
  • Hypertext
  • Hyperlinks

Website

 

  • Website is the collection of webpages , associated with a particular person, business, government school and organisation.
  • Information can be on a single page or multiple pages.
  • Websites consist of a number of webpages that help with a large amount of information. 
  • Various types of websites are available on the internet. 

Example- jobs, education etc. 

Webpages

  • A web page is an electronic document written in HTML language. 
  • It is accessible through the Internet using a browser.
  • Each webpage has a unique address called URL.
  • The first page of any website is known as the homepage. 
  • A web page is accessed by entering URL or main content text, graphic, audio video, etc. 
  • Web Page is part of any website. 

Hyperlinks

It is the web navigation element that allows users to move or navigate between web pages.

It is also used to download audio, video and other types of files.

Generally Hyperlinks are shown in blue underline that has three types-

  1. Text Hyperlink
  2. Image Hyperlink
  3. Image maps

Hypertext

A web page text that contains a hyperlink is known as hypertext.
